title.zh: 卷八十 列傳第五 太宗諸子
title.raw: 卷八十 列傳第五 太宗諸子 Volume 80 Biographies 5: Sons of Taizu

sentences.zh: 太宗諸子

translations.literal: The various sons of Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: The Sons of Emperor Taizong

sentences.zh: 太宗十四子：文德皇后生承乾，又生第四子泰、高宗皇帝，后宮生寬，楊妃生恪，又生第六子愔，陰妃生祐，王氏生惲，燕妃生貞，又生第十一子囂，韋妃生慎，後宮生簡，楊妃生福，楊氏生明。

translations.literal: Taizong had fourteen sons: Empress Wende bore Chengqian, and also bore the fourth son Tai and the Emperor Gaozong; a rear-palace consort bore Kuan; Consort Yang bore Ke, and also bore the sixth son Yin; Consort Yin bore You; Lady Wang bore Yun; Consort Yan bore Zhen, and also bore the eleventh son Xiao; Consort Wei bore Shen; a rear-palace consort bore Jian; Consort Yang bore Fu; Lady Yang bore Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong had fourteen sons: Empress Wende gave birth to Chengqian, and also to his fourth son Li Tai and to the future Emperor Gaozong; a palace consort bore Kuan; Consort Yang bore Ke and also his sixth son Yin; Consort Yin bore You; Lady Wang bore Yun; Consort Yan bore Zhen and also his eleventh son Xiao; Consort Wei bore Shen; a palace consort bore Jian; Consort Yang bore Fu; and Lady Yang bore Ming.

sentences.zh: 常山湣王承乾字高明，生承乾殿，即以命之。

translations.literal: The Lamented Prince of Changshan, Chengqian, styled Gaoming, was born in Chengqian Hall, and was named thereby.
translations.idiomatic: The Lamented Prince of Changshan, Chengqian, whose courtesy name was Gaoming, was born in Chengqian Hall, and received his name from that place.

sentences.zh: 武德三年，始王常山郡，與長沙、宜都二王同封。

translations.literal: In the third year of Wude he was first enfeoffed as Prince of Changshan commandery, together with the Princes of Changsha and Yidu receiving investiture at the same time.
translations.idiomatic: In 620, he was first enfeoffed as Prince of Changshan, receiving his title on the same occasion as the Princes of Changsha and Yidu.

sentences.zh: 俄徙中山。

translations.literal: Shortly he was transferred to Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，立為皇太子。

translations.literal: When Taizong took the throne, he was established as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong ascended the throne, Chengqian was installed as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 甫八歲，特敏惠，帝愛之。

translations.literal: At only eight years he was exceptionally clever and perceptive, and the emperor loved him.
translations.idiomatic: At only eight years old he proved exceptionally quick-witted, and the emperor doted on him.

sentences.zh: 在諒暗，使裁決庶政，有大體，後每行幸，則令監國。

translations.literal: During the mourning period he was made to decide ordinary government affairs and showed a grasp of essentials; afterward, whenever the emperor went on tour, he was ordered to oversee the state.
translations.idiomatic: During the mourning period for Empress Wende, he was entrusted to decide routine state affairs and showed sound judgment; thereafter, whenever the emperor traveled, he was left to supervise the realm.

sentences.zh: 及長，好聲色慢遊，然懼帝，秘其跡。

translations.literal: When he grew up, he loved music, women, and idle roaming, yet feared the emperor and concealed his tracks.
translations.idiomatic: As he grew older, he took to music, women, and dissolute wandering, but fearing his father, he kept these pursuits hidden.

sentences.zh: 臨朝，言諄諄必忠孝，退乃與群不逞狎慢。

translations.literal: At court audience his words were earnest and always on loyalty and filial piety; in retirement he consorted familiarly and insolently with a crowd of unruly men.
translations.idiomatic: In audience he spoke earnestly of loyalty and filial duty, but once he withdrew he caroused familiarly with a band of dissolute companions.

sentences.zh: 左右或進諫，危坐斂容，痛自咎，飾非辯給，諫者拜答不暇，故人人以為賢而莫之察。

translations.literal: When attendants sometimes offered remonstrance, he would sit upright and compose his countenance, bitterly blaming himself, adorn his faults with clever argument, and bow in reply to remonstrators without pause; therefore everyone thought him worthy and none perceived the truth.
translations.idiomatic: When his attendants ventured to remonstrate, he would sit bolt upright, compose his features, and blame himself bitterly, masking his faults with glib argument and bowing to his critics without pause—so that everyone took him for virtuous and none saw through him.

sentences.zh: 後過惡寢聞，宮臣若孔穎達、令狐德棻、于志寧、張玄素、趙弘智、王仁表、崔知機等皆天下選，每規爭承乾，帝必厚賜金帛，欲以厲其心。

translations.literal: Later his faults and evils gradually became known. Palace officials such as Kong Yingda, Linghu Defen, Yu Zhining, Zhang Xuansu, Zhao Hongzhi, Wang Renbiao, and Cui Zhiji were all chosen from the empire; each would admonish and dispute with Chengqian, and the emperor would invariably bestow gold and silk in abundance, wishing thereby to sharpen his mind.
translations.idiomatic: As his misconduct gradually came to light, the palace tutors Kong Yingda, Linghu Defen, Yu Zhining, Zhang Xuansu, Zhao Hongzhi, Wang Renbiao, and Cui Zhiji—men chosen from the finest in the realm—repeatedly admonished him. The emperor always rewarded them lavishly with gold and silk, hoping to spur the crown prince's conscience.

sentences.zh: 承乾慠不悛，往往遣人陰圖害之。

translations.literal: Chengqian was arrogant and would not reform, and often sent men to plot secretly to harm them.
translations.idiomatic: Chengqian remained arrogant and unrepentant, and often sent men to plot secretly against them.

sentences.zh: 時魏王泰有美名，帝愛重。

translations.literal: At that time Prince of Wei Tai had a fine reputation, and the emperor loved and valued him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Prince of Wei Li Tai enjoyed a fine reputation, and the emperor favored him deeply.

sentences.zh: 而承乾病足，不良行，且懼廢，與泰交惡。

translations.literal: But Chengqian's feet were afflicted and he walked poorly, and moreover he feared deposition; he and Tai became mutually hostile.
translations.idiomatic: Chengqian, however, suffered from a crippled foot and walked with difficulty; fearing deposition, he grew hostile toward Li Tai.

sentences.zh: 泰亦謀奪長，各樹黨。

translations.literal: Tai also plotted to seize the senior position, and each built up factions.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tai likewise plotted to supplant his elder brother, and each cultivated his own faction.

sentences.zh: 東宮有俳兒，善姿首，承乾嬖愛，帝聞震怒，收兒殺之，坐死者數人。

translations.literal: In the Eastern Palace there was a boy actor skilled in bearing and appearance whom Chengqian doted on. When the emperor heard of it he was shaken with rage, seized the boy and killed him, and several persons were put to death on account of it.
translations.idiomatic: A boy actor in the Eastern Palace, gifted in looks and carriage, became Chengqian's favorite. When the emperor learned of it he flew into a rage, seized the boy and executed him, and several others were put to death in connection with the affair.

sentences.zh: 承乾意為泰告，望甚。

translations.literal: Chengqian supposed that Tai had informed against him and looked upon him with great resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Chengqian believed Li Tai had denounced him and regarded him with bitter resentment.

sentences.zh: 內念兒不已，築室圖其象，贈官樹碑，為起冢苑中，朝夕祭。

translations.literal: Inwardly he thought of the boy without cease, built a chamber with his likeness painted, granted him an official title and erected a stele, raised a tomb for him within the park, and offered sacrifice morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: He could not stop thinking of the boy. He built a chamber bearing his portrait, posthumously granted him an office and erected a stele, raised a tomb for him in the palace park, and made offerings morning and evening.

sentences.zh: 承乾至其處裴回，涕數行下，愈怨懟，稱疾不朝，累數月。

translations.literal: Chengqian would come to the place and linger, tears streaming down many lines; his resentment grew ever sharper. He claimed illness and did not attend court for many months in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Chengqian would linger at the tomb, tears streaming down his face, his resentment deepening. He pleaded illness and absented himself from court for months on end.

sentences.zh: 又使戶奴數十百人習音聲，學胡人椎髻，剪彩為舞衣，尋橦跳劍，鼓鞞聲通晝夜不絕。

translations.literal: He also made several tens or hundreds of household slaves learn music and song, study the topknot of the Hu, cut colored silk for dance garments, practice pole-climbing and sword-dancing, and drum and beat so that the sound ran unbroken day and night.
translations.idiomatic: He also set several dozen household slaves to learning music, imitating the topknots of the Turks, cutting colored silk for dance costumes, practicing pole-climbing and sword dances—the drumming and beating resounding without cease day and night.

sentences.zh: 造大銅爐、六熟鼎，招亡奴盜取人牛馬，親視烹燖，召所幸廝養共食之。

translations.literal: He made a great bronze cauldron and the Six Ripe Tripods, recruited absconded slaves to steal people's cattle and horses, personally watched the boiling and roasting, and summoned his favored attendants to eat together.
translations.idiomatic: He had a great bronze cauldron and the Six Tripods made, recruited runaway slaves to steal cattle and horses, personally supervised the cooking, and summoned his favorite attendants to feast with him.

sentences.zh: 又好突厥言及所服，選貌類胡者，被以羊裘，辮髪，五人建一落，張氈舍，造五狼頭纛，分戟為陣，系幡旗，設穹廬自居，使諸部斂羊以烹，抽佩刀割肉相啗。

translations.literal: He also loved Turkic speech and dress, chose men whose appearance resembled the Hu, clothed them in sheepskin coats with braided hair, five men forming one encampment; spread felt tents, made a banner of five wolf heads, divided spears into formations, hung pennants and flags, set up a yurt and dwelt in it himself, and had the various divisions gather sheep to cook, drawing their belt knives to cut meat and eat one another's portions.
translations.idiomatic: He also took to Turkic language and dress, selecting men who looked Turkic, clothing them in sheepskins with braided hair, five to a camp. He pitched felt tents, fashioned a banner with five wolf heads, arrayed spears in formations with pennants flying, set up a yurt for himself, and had his followers gather sheep for cooking, drawing their belt knives to cut meat and eat together.

sentences.zh: 承乾身作可汗死。

translations.literal: Chengqian himself played the khan's death.
translations.idiomatic: Chengqian himself played the part of a dying khan.

sentences.zh: 使眾號哭剺面，奔馬環臨之。

translations.literal: He made the crowd wail and slash their faces, and galloping horses circle around him.
translations.idiomatic: He had his followers wail and gash their faces while horsemen galloped in circles around him.

sentences.zh: 忽復起曰：「使我有天下，將數萬騎到金城，然後解發，委身思摩，當一設，顧不快邪！」

translations.literal: Suddenly he rose again and said: "If I had the realm under heaven, I would lead tens of thousands of horsemen to Jincheng, then let down my hair, entrust myself to Simo, and have one feast—would that not be a delight!"
translations.idiomatic: Then he would suddenly rise and say, "If I possessed the realm, I would lead tens of thousands of horsemen to Jincheng, then let down my hair and submit myself to Simo for a great feast—would that not be splendid!"

sentences.zh: 左右私相語，以為妖。

translations.literal: Those about him privately spoke to one another, considering it demonic.
translations.idiomatic: His attendants whispered among themselves that he had gone mad.

sentences.zh: 又襞氈為鎧，列丹幟，勒部陣，與漢王元昌分統，大呼擊刺為樂。

translations.literal: He also folded felt into armor, arrayed cinnabar banners, drilled the divisions in formation, and with Prince of Han Yuan-chang divided command, shouting loudly and striking and stabbing for amusement.
translations.idiomatic: He also folded felt into armor, set out crimson banners, drilled his followers in formation, and with Prince of Han Li Yuan-chang divided command between them, shouting and thrusting at one another for sport.

sentences.zh: 不用命者，披樹抶之，或至死，輕者輒腐之。

translations.literal: Those who did not obey orders he would strip and beat against trees, sometimes to death; the lighter cases he would simply flog until they rotted.
translations.idiomatic: Those who disobeyed he would strip and beat against trees, sometimes to death; lesser offenders he would flog until their flesh was raw.

sentences.zh: 嘗曰：「我作天子，當肆吾欲；

translations.literal: He once said: "If I become Son of Heaven, I shall indulge my desires to the full;
translations.idiomatic: He once said, "When I become emperor, I shall indulge every desire;

sentences.zh: 有諫者，我殺之，殺五百人，豈不定？」

translations.literal: if there are remonstrators, I shall kill them—kill five hundred men, and will the realm not be settled?"
translations.idiomatic: if anyone remonstrates, I shall kill him—kill five hundred men, and will the realm not be secure?"

sentences.zh: 又召壯士左衛副率封師進、刺客張師政、紇幹承基等謀殺魏王泰，不克，遂與元昌、侯君集、李安儼、趙節、杜荷镵臂血之，謀以兵入西宮。

translations.literal: He also summoned stalwarts—the Left Guard vice-commander Feng Shijin, the assassin Zhang Shizheng, Qagan Chenji, and others—to plot killing Prince of Wei Tai; it did not succeed. Thereupon with Yuan-chang, Hou Junji, Li Anyan, Zhao Jie, and Du He he cut arms and mingled blood, plotting to enter the Western Palace with troops.
translations.idiomatic: He also summoned stalwarts—the Left Guard vice-commander Feng Shijin, the assassin Zhang Shizheng, and Qagan Chenji among others—to plot the murder of Prince of Wei Li Tai, but the attempt failed. He then cut arms and mingled blood with Li Yuan-chang, Hou Junji, Li Anyan, Zhao Jie, and Du He, plotting to lead troops into the Western Palace.

sentences.zh: 貞觀十七年，齊王祐反齊州，承乾謂承基等：「我宮西墻，去大內正可二十步棘耳，豈與齊州等？」

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Zhenguan, Prince of Qi You rebelled at Qizhou. Chengqian said to Chenji and the others: "The western wall of my palace is only twenty paces of thorn hedge from the Great Within—how can that be compared with Qizhou?"
translations.idiomatic: In 643, when Prince of Qi Li You rebelled at Qizhou, Chengqian told Chenji and the others, "The western wall of my palace is only twenty paces of thorn hedge from the Inner Palace—how can that compare with Qizhou?"

sentences.zh: 會承基連齊王事繫獄當死，即上變。

translations.literal: It happened that Chenji, implicated in the affair of Prince of Qi, was imprisoned and faced death; he immediately submitted a secret report.
translations.idiomatic: As it happened, Chenji, implicated in Prince of Qi's rebellion, was imprisoned and faced execution; he immediately submitted a secret denunciation.

sentences.zh: 帝詔長孫無忌、房玄齡、蕭瑀、李勣、孫伏伽、岑文本、馬周、褚遂良雜治，廢為庶人，徙黔州。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Zhangsun Wuji, Fang Xuanling, Xiao Yu, Li Jing, Sun Fuga, Cen Wende, Ma Zhou, and Chu Suiliang jointly to try the case. Chengqian was deposed to commoner status and exiled to Qianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Zhangsun Wuji, Fang Xuanling, Xiao Yu, Li Jing, Sun Fuga, Cen Wende, Ma Zhou, and Chu Suiliang jointly to investigate. Chengqian was deposed to commoner status and exiled to Qianzhou.

sentences.zh: 十九年死，帝為廢朝，葬以國公禮。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he died; the emperor suspended court for him and buried him with the rites of a state duke.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 645. The emperor suspended court in mourning and buried him with the rites due a state duke.

sentences.zh: 子象，為懷州別駕，厥鄂州別駕。

translations.literal: His sons Xiang served as vice-prefect of Huaizhou, and Jue as vice-prefect of Ezhou.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Xiang served as vice-prefect of Huaizhou and Jue as vice-prefect of Ezhou.

sentences.zh: 開元中，象子適之為宰相，贈還承乾始王，象越州都督、郇國公。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan era, Xiang's son Shizhi became chancellor; posthumous honors were restored to Chengqian's original princely title, and Xiang was made Governor of Yuezhou and Duke of Xun.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaiyuan reign, Xiang's son Li Shizhi became chancellor; Chengqian's original princely title was posthumously restored, and Xiang was appointed Governor of Yuezhou and enfeoffed as Duke of Xun.

sentences.zh: 郁林王恪，始王長沙，俄進封漢。

translations.literal: Prince of Yulin Ke was first enfeoffed as Prince of Changsha, and shortly advanced to Prince of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Yulin Li Ke was first enfeoffed as Prince of Changsha, then soon advanced to Prince of Han.

sentences.zh: 貞觀二年徙蜀，與越、燕二王同封。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenguan he was transferred to Shu, receiving investiture together with the Princes of Yue and Yan.
translations.idiomatic: In 628 he was transferred to Prince of Shu, receiving his title together with the Princes of Yue and Yan.

sentences.zh: 不之國，久乃為齊州都督。

translations.literal: He did not go to his domain; only after a long time was he made Governor of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He did not proceed to his fief; only after a long interval was he appointed Governor of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 帝謂左右曰：』吾於恪豈不欲常見之？

translations.literal: The emperor said to those about him: "As for Ke, would I not wish to see him constantly?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to his attendants, "As for Ke, would I not wish to see him constantly?

sentences.zh: 但令早有定分，使外作籓屏，吾百歲後，庶兄弟無危亡憂。」

translations.literal: But if they are given their allotted stations early and made to serve abroad as screen and shield, after my hundred years my brothers in the main will have no fear of peril and ruin."
translations.idiomatic: But if they are assigned their stations early and sent out to serve as frontier shields, after my death my brothers should have no fear of ruin."

sentences.zh: 十年，改王吳，與魏、齊、蜀、蔣、越、紀六王同徙封。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was changed to Prince of Wu, together with the six princes of Wei, Qi, Shu, Jiang, Yue, and Ji receiving transferred investiture at the same time.
translations.idiomatic: In 636 he was transferred to Prince of Wu, together with the Princes of Wei, Qi, Shu, Jiang, Yue, and Ji receiving new titles on the same occasion.

sentences.zh: 授安州都督。

translations.literal: He was appointed Governor of Anzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Governor of Anzhou.

sentences.zh: 帝賜書曰：「汝惟茂親，勉思所以籓王室，以義制事，以禮制心。

translations.literal: The emperor bestowed a letter saying: "You are a close kinsman of flourishing degree; strive to consider how to shield the royal house, regulate affairs by righteousness, and regulate the heart by ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wrote him: "As a close kinsman of the highest rank, strive to shield the royal house—govern your conduct by righteousness and your heart by ritual.

sentences.zh: 外之為君臣，內之為父子，今當去膝下，不遺汝珍，而遺汝以言，其念之哉！」

translations.literal: Outwardly you are minister and lord; inwardly you are father and son. Now you must leave my knee; I do not bequeath you treasures, but bequeath you words—ponder them well!"
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly we are sovereign and subject; inwardly we are father and son. Now you must leave my side. I bequeath you not treasures but words—ponder them well!"

sentences.zh: 坐與乳媼子博塞，罷都督，削封戶三百。

translations.literal: For the offense of gambling with his wet nurse's son, he was dismissed as governor and three hundred fief households were struck from his enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: For gambling with his wet nurse's son, he was dismissed as governor and three hundred fief households were struck from his enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，拜司空、梁州都督。

translations.literal: When Gaozong took the throne, Ke was appointed Minister of Works and Governor of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong ascended the throne, Ke was appointed Minister of Works and Governor of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 恪善騎射，有文武才。

translations.literal: Ke was skilled in horsemanship and archery and possessed both civil and military talent.
translations.idiomatic: Ke excelled at horsemanship and archery and possessed both civil and military talent.

sentences.zh: 其母隋煬帝女，地親望高，中外所向。

translations.literal: His mother was a daughter of Emperor Yang of Sui; his station was close in kinship and high in prestige, and both within and without the court looked toward him.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was a daughter of Emperor Yang of Sui; by birth and reputation he stood high, and court and country alike looked to him.

sentences.zh: 帝初以晉王為太子，又欲立恪，長孫無忌固爭，帝曰：「公豈以非己甥邪？

translations.literal: The emperor had first made Prince of Jin crown prince, yet also wished to establish Ke. Zhangsun Wuji firmly disputed it. The emperor said: "Are you perhaps displeased that he is not your own nephew?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had first installed Prince of Jin as crown prince, yet also wished to make Ke heir. Zhangsun Wuji firmly opposed it. The emperor said, "Are you displeased that he is not your own nephew?

sentences.zh: 且兒英果類我，若保護舅氏，未可知。」

translations.literal: Moreover the boy is spirited and resolute like me; if he should protect his maternal uncles' house, that cannot be foreknown."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the boy is spirited and resolute like me; if he were to protect your clan, who can say what might happen?"

sentences.zh: 無忌曰：「晉王仁厚，守文之良主，且舉棋不定則敗，況儲位乎？」

translations.literal: Wuji said: "Prince of Jin is benevolent and generous—a fine ruler to preserve the written patrimony. Moreover, if in moving chess pieces one is undecided, one is defeated—how much more the heir's position?"
translations.idiomatic: Wuji replied, "Prince of Jin is benevolent and magnanimous—a fine ruler to preserve the patrimony. Moreover, hesitation at chess loses the game—how much more the heir's position?"

sentences.zh: 帝乃止。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon desisted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thereupon abandoned the idea.

sentences.zh: 故無忌常惡之。

translations.literal: Therefore Wuji constantly hated him.
translations.idiomatic: From that time Wuji bore him constant enmity.

sentences.zh: 永徽中，房遺愛謀反，因遂誅恪，以絕天下望。

translations.literal: In the Yonghui era, when Fang Yiai plotted rebellion, Ke was thereupon executed to cut off the hopes of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yonghui reign, when Fang Yiai plotted rebellion, Ke was executed on that pretext to extinguish the hopes the realm had placed in him.

sentences.zh: 臨刑呼曰：「社稷有靈，無忌且族滅！」

translations.literal: Facing execution he cried out: "If the altars of state have spirits, Wuji will soon be exterminated to the last of his clan!"
translations.idiomatic: Facing execution he cried out, "If the altars of state have spirits, Wuji will soon be exterminated to the last of his clan!"

sentences.zh: 四子，仁、瑋、琨、璄並流嶺表。

translations.literal: His four sons Ren, Wei, Kun, and Jue were all exiled beyond the Ling Mountains.
translations.idiomatic: His four sons Ren, Wei, Kun, and Jue were all exiled to the far south.

sentences.zh: 顯慶五年，追王郁林，為立廟，以河間王孝恭孫榮為郁林縣侯以嗣。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xianqing he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Yulin, a temple was established for him, and Rong, grandson of Prince of Hejian Li Xiaogong, was made Marquis of Yulin county as heir.
translations.idiomatic: In 660 he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Yulin, a temple was established for him, and Rong, grandson of Prince of Hejian Li Xiaogong, was made Marquis of Yulin to continue his line.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，贈司空，備禮改葬。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong he was posthumously given Minister of Works and reburied with full rites.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Shenlong reign he was posthumously appointed Minister of Works and reburied with full honors.

sentences.zh: 光宅中，仁遇赦還，適會榮以罪斥，故得襲郁林縣男，歷岳州別駕，爵郡公。

translations.literal: In the Guangzhai era, Ren encountered an amnesty and returned; it happened that Rong was dismissed for a crime, so Ren was able to inherit as Baron of Yulin county, served successively as vice-prefect of Yuezhou, and held the noble rank of Duke of a commandery.
translations.idiomatic: During the Guangzhai reign, Ren returned under an amnesty; as Rong had been dismissed for a crime, Ren was able to inherit as Baron of Yulin, served as vice-prefect of Yuezhou, and rose to the rank of commandery duke.

sentences.zh: 嘗使江左，州人遺以金，拒不內。

translations.literal: Once when sent on mission to the lands south of the Yangzi, the people of the prefecture presented him with gold; he refused to accept it.
translations.idiomatic: Once when sent on mission to the lower Yangzi region, the local people offered him gold; he refused to accept it.

sentences.zh: 武后遣使者勞曰：「兒，吾家千里駒。」

translations.literal: Empress Wu sent an envoy to comfort him, saying: "My son, you are our family's thousand-li colt."
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu sent an envoy to commend him, saying, "My son, you are our family's thousand-li steed."

sentences.zh: 更名千里。

translations.literal: His name was changed to Qianli.
translations.idiomatic: His name was changed to Qianli (Thousand Li).

sentences.zh: 自天授後，宗室賢者多株剪，唯千里詭躁不情，數進符瑞諸異物，得免。

translations.literal: From the Tian-shou reign onward, many worthy members of the imperial clan were cut down; only Qianli, crafty, restless, and unfeeling, repeatedly presented talismans, auspicious omens, and various strange objects, and thereby escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: From the Tian-shou reign onward, many worthy members of the imperial clan were destroyed; only Qianli, crafty and unscrupulous, survived by repeatedly presenting omens, talismans, and curiosities.

sentences.zh: 中宗反正，改王成紀。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong restored the correct order, he was changed to Prince of Chengji.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhongzong was restored, Qianli was made Prince of Chengji.

sentences.zh: 未幾，進王成。

translations.literal: Before long he was advanced to Prince of Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was advanced to Prince of Cheng.

sentences.zh: 節湣太子誅武三思，千里與其子天水王禧率數十人斬右延明門以入。

translations.literal: When the Lamented and Stern Crown Prince killed Wu Sansi, Qianli with his son Prince of Tianshui Xi led several tens of men to cut through the Right Yanming Gate and enter.
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Jiemin killed Wu Sansi, Qianli and his son Prince of Tianshui Xi led several dozen men to cut through the Right Yanming Gate and enter.

sentences.zh: 太子敗，誅死，籍其家，改氏「蝮」。

translations.literal: The crown prince was defeated; Qianli was executed to death, his household was registered for confiscation, and the clan name was changed to "Viper."
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince was defeated, Qianli was executed, his property confiscated, and his clan name changed to "Viper."

sentences.zh: 睿宗立，詔還氏及官爵。

translations.literal: When Ruizong took the throne, an edict restored the clan name and offices and ranks.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ruizong took the throne, an edict restored the clan name and his offices and titles.

sentences.zh: 瑋蚤卒，中宗追封朗陵王。

translations.literal: Wei died young; Zhongzong posthumously enfeoffed him as Prince of Langling.
translations.idiomatic: Wei died young; Emperor Zhongzong posthumously enfeoffed him as Prince of Langling.

sentences.zh: 子礻玄，出繼蜀王愔。

translations.literal: His son Xuan went out to continue the line of Prince of Shu Yin.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xuan was adopted to continue the line of Prince of Shu Li Yin.

sentences.zh: 開元中，以傍繼國改封廣漢郡王，遷太僕卿同正員，薨。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan era, because he continued a collateral line's state, he was changed to Prince of Guanghan commandery, promoted to Minister of the Stud with the same regular status, and died.
translations.idiomatic: During Kaiyuan, as an heir from a collateral line he was made Prince of Guanghan, appointed Minister of the Stud with regular status, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 琨，武后時歷六州刺史，皆有名。

translations.literal: Kun, during Empress Wu's time, served successively as governor of six prefectures, all with reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Kun served successively as governor of six prefectures under Empress Wu, earning a reputation in each.

sentences.zh: 聖歷中，為嶺南招慰使，安輯反獠，甚得其宜。

translations.literal: In the Shenli era he was Commissioner to Pacify and Console Lingnan, soothing and gathering rebellious Liao tribesmen, and handled it with great fitness.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shenli reign he served as Commissioner to Pacify Lingnan, pacifying rebellious tribal peoples with notable success.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈司衛卿。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously given Minister of the Guards.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously appointed Minister of the Guards.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，贈張掖郡王。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong he was posthumously given Prince of Zhangye commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Shenlong reign he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Zhangye.

sentences.zh: 開元中，以子祎貴，追封吳王。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan era, because his son Yi became eminent, he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: During Kaiyuan, because his son Li Yi rose to prominence, Kun was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Wu.

sentences.zh: 祎少有誌尚，事繼母謹，撫異母弟祗，以友稱。

translations.literal: Yi from youth had aspiration and resolve; he served his stepmother with care, nurtured his younger half-brother Zhi, and was known for friendship.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Yi showed ambition and principle; he served his stepmother dutifully and cared for his younger half-brother Zhi, earning renown for brotherly devotion.

sentences.zh: 當襲封，固讓祗，中宗嘉其意，特封嗣江王，以繼囂後。

translations.literal: When he was due to inherit the enfeoffment, he firmly yielded to Zhi; Zhongzong commended his intent and specially enfeoffed him as Prince of Sijiang to continue Xiao's line.
translations.idiomatic: When his turn came to inherit, he firmly yielded to Zhi; Emperor Zhongzong commended his generosity and specially enfeoffed him as Prince of Sijiang to continue Prince Xiao's line.

sentences.zh: 開元時，亦以傍繼徙信安郡王。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan era, likewise because he continued a collateral line, he was transferred to Prince of Xin'an commandery.
translations.idiomatic: During Kaiyuan, as heir from a collateral line, he was transferred to Prince of Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 累為州刺史，治嚴辦。

translations.literal: He served repeatedly as prefectural governor, governing with severity and efficiency.
translations.idiomatic: He served repeatedly as prefectural governor, governing with severity and efficiency.

sentences.zh: 遷禮部尚書、朔方節度使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Rites and Military Commissioner of Shuofang.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Minister of Rites and Military Commissioner of Shuofang.

sentences.zh: 初，吐蕃據石堡城，數盜塞，詔祎與河西、隴右議攻取。

translations.literal: Earlier the Tibetans had occupied Shibao Fortress and repeatedly raided the border passes; an edict ordered Yi together with Hexi and Longyou to deliberate on attacking and taking it.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Tibetans had occupied Shibao Fortress and repeatedly raided the frontier; the court ordered Yi, together with the Hexi and Longyou commands, to plan its capture.

sentences.zh: 既到屯，諏日進師。

translations.literal: Once he reached the encampment, he chose a day to advance the army.
translations.idiomatic: Once his forces were encamped, he chose a day to advance.

sentences.zh: 或謂：「城險，賊所愛，必固守。

translations.literal: Some said: "The fortress is perilous and beloved of the enemy; they will surely hold it firmly.
translations.idiomatic: Some advised him, "The fortress is perilous and the enemy prizes it—they will surely defend it stubbornly.

sentences.zh: 今兵深入，有如不捷，吾軍必奔，不如持重伺賊勢。」

translations.literal: Now that the army has penetrated deep, if we do not succeed our forces will surely flee—it is better to hold steady and watch the enemy's disposition."
translations.idiomatic: Our army has penetrated deep; if we fail, our troops will surely flee. Better to hold steady and watch the enemy's movements."

sentences.zh: 祎曰：「人臣之節，豈憚險不進乎？

translations.literal: Yi said: "A subject's duty—how can one fear peril and not advance?
translations.idiomatic: Yi replied, "A subject's duty—how can one shrink from peril and refuse to advance?

sentences.zh: 必眾寡不敵者，吾以死繼之。」

translations.literal: If we must be outmatched in numbers, I shall follow with my death."
translations.idiomatic: If we are outnumbered, I shall die in the attempt."

sentences.zh: 於是分兵迮賊路，督諸將倍道進，遂拔之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he divided troops to block the enemy's routes, urged the generals to advance by double marches, and thus captured it.
translations.idiomatic: He then divided his forces to block the enemy's escape routes, urged his generals to advance at forced march, and captured the fortress.

sentences.zh: 自是河、隴諸軍遊弈，拓地至千里。

translations.literal: From this the armies of He and Longyou patrolled and extended territory to a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the armies of the Yellow River and Longyou regions patrolled freely, extending Tang territory by a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 玄宗喜，更號其城曰振武軍。

translations.literal: Xuanzong was pleased and renamed the fortress Zhenwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong was delighted and renamed the fortress Zhenwu Army.

sentences.zh: 契丹牙官可突於叛，詔拜忠王為河北道行軍元帥討之，敕祎以副。

translations.literal: The Khitan yabghu Ketuyu rebelled; an edict appointed Prince of Zhong as Grand Marshal of the Hebei campaign army to suppress him, and ordered Yi as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan chieftain Ketuyu rebelled, the court appointed Prince of Zhong grand marshal of the Hebei campaign to suppress him, with Yi as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 王不行，故祎率裴耀卿諸將分道出范陽北，擊二蕃，破之，禽酋長以還，余部竄伏。

translations.literal: The prince did not go; therefore Yi led Pei Yaoji and the other generals in separate columns north of Fanyang, struck the two barbarian peoples, defeated them, captured the chieftain and returned, and the remaining bands scattered and hid.
translations.idiomatic: The prince did not take the field, so Yi led Pei Yaoji and other generals in separate columns north of Fanyang, defeated the Khitan and Xi forces, captured their chieftain, and returned while the remnants scattered into hiding.

sentences.zh: 加開府儀同三司，領關內支度營田采訪處置使，授二子官。

translations.literal: He was given the rank of Grandee of the State with privilege of the same Three Excellencies as the Three Dukes, made Commissioner for Support, Military Farms, Investigation, and Disposition within Guannei, and his two sons were granted offices.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Grandee of the State with privilege equal to the Three Excellencies, appointed Commissioner for Support, Military Farms, Investigation, and Disposition within Guannei, and his two sons were granted offices.

sentences.zh: 祎功多，執政害之，賞不讎，為當時所恨。

translations.literal: Yi's achievements were many, but those in power envied him; rewards did not match his merits, and he was resented by contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's achievements were many, but those in power envied him; his rewards never matched his merits, to the resentment of his contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 久之，擢兵部尚書，為朔方節度大使。

translations.literal: After a long time he was promoted to Minister of War and made Grand Military Commissioner of Shuofang.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was promoted to Minister of War and appointed Grand Military Commissioner of Shuofang.

sentences.zh: 坐事下除衢州刺史。

translations.literal: For an offense he was demoted and made Prefect of Quzhou.
translations.idiomatic: For an offense he was demoted to Prefect of Quzhou.

sentences.zh: 歷滑、懷二州。

translations.literal: He served successively in the two prefectures of Hua and Huai.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as prefect of Hua and Huai.

sentences.zh: 天寶初，以太子少師致仕。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao he retired on account of Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tianbao reign he retired as Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 明年，遷太師，未拜，薨。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to Grand Preceptor but had not received investiture when he died.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was promoted to Grand Preceptor but died before he could assume the office.

sentences.zh: 祎治家嚴，教子有法度，故峘、嶧、峴皆顯。

translations.literal: Yi governed the household strictly and taught his sons with method and measure; therefore Han, Yi, and Xian all became eminent.
translations.idiomatic: Yi ran his household with strict discipline and raised his sons with proper standards; consequently Han, Yi, and Xian all rose to prominence.

sentences.zh: 濮恭王泰字惠褒。

translations.literal: The Respectful Prince of Pu, Tai, styled Huibao.
translations.idiomatic: The Respectful Prince of Pu, Li Tai, whose courtesy name was Huibao.

sentences.zh: 始王宜都，徙封衛，繼懷王後。

translations.literal: He was first enfeoffed as Prince of Yidu, then transferred to Prince of Wei, continuing the line of Prince of Huai.
translations.idiomatic: He was first enfeoffed as Prince of Yidu, then transferred to Prince of Wei to continue the line of Prince of Huai.

sentences.zh: 又徙封越，為揚州大都督。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Prince of Yue and made Grand Governor of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was again transferred to Prince of Yue and appointed Grand Governor of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 再遷雍州牧、左武候大將軍。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Governor of Yongzhou and Grand General of the Left Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was further appointed Governor of Yongzhou and Grand General of the Left Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 改王魏。

translations.literal: He was changed to Prince of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Prince of Wei.

sentences.zh: 帝以泰好士，善屬文，詔即府置文學館，得自引學士。

translations.literal: Because the emperor considered Tai fond of scholars and skilled in literary composition, he ordered that a Literary Academy be established at his princely residence, and Tai was permitted to recruit academicians himself.
translations.idiomatic: Because the emperor saw that Tai loved scholars and excelled at writing, he ordered a Literary Academy established at Tai's residence, allowing him to recruit scholars on his own authority.

sentences.zh: 又以泰大腰腹，聽乘小輿至朝。

translations.literal: Moreover, because Tai had a large waist and belly, he was permitted to ride in a small palanquin to court.
translations.idiomatic: Because Tai was corpulent, he was also permitted to ride in a small palanquin to audience.

sentences.zh: 司馬蘇勖勸泰延賓客著書，如古賢王。

translations.literal: His Chief Administrator Su Xu urged Tai to invite guests and compile books, like the sage kings of old.
translations.idiomatic: His chief administrator Su Xu urged Tai to gather guests and compile books, emulating the sage kings of antiquity.

sentences.zh: 泰乃奏撰《括地志》，於是引著作郎蕭德言、秘書郎顧胤、記室參軍蔣亞卿、功曹參軍謝偃等撰次。

translations.literal: Tai thereupon memorialized to compile the Comprehensive Gazetteer of the Realm, and thus recruited Compiler Xiao Deyan, Secretary Gu Yin, Recorder Jiang Yaqing, Registrar Xie Yan, and others to arrange and edit it.
translations.idiomatic: Tai thereupon memorialized to compile the Comprehensive Gazetteer of the Realm, recruiting Compiler Xiao Deyan, Secretary Gu Yin, Recorder Jiang Yaqing, Registrar Xie Yan, and others to organize the work.

sentences.zh: 衛尉供帳，光祿給食，士有文學者多與，而貴遊子弟更相因藉，門若市然。

translations.literal: The Commandant of the Guard supplied lodging, the Minister of Imperial Entertainments provided food, and many men of literary learning joined him; moreover, sons of noble families relied on one another in succession, and his gate was like a market.
translations.idiomatic: The Commandant of the Guard supplied lodging and the Minister of Imperial Entertainments provided food; many literary men joined him, and sons of noble families flocked to his gate until it resembled a marketplace.

sentences.zh: 泰悟其過，欲速成，乃分道計州，繙緝疏錄，凡五百五十篇，歷四期成。

translations.literal: Tai perceived his excess and wished to finish quickly; he therefore divided routes to tally the prefectures, turned and compiled summaries and records, five hundred fifty sections in all, completed over four seasons.
translations.idiomatic: Tai perceived his extravagance and wished to finish quickly; he divided the work by route to survey each prefecture, compiling summaries and records—five hundred fifty sections in all, completed in four seasons.

sentences.zh: 詔藏秘閣，所賜萬段。

translations.literal: An edict ordered it stored in the Secret Archive; he was granted ten thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the work stored in the Secret Archive and granted him ten thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 後帝幸泰延康坊第，曲赦長安死罪，免坊人一年租，府僚以差賜帛。

translations.literal: Later the emperor visited Tai's residence in Yankang Ward, granted a special amnesty for capital crimes in Chang'an, exempted the ward's people from one year's rent, and bestowed silk on the princely staff according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: Later the emperor visited Tai's residence in Yankang Ward, granted a special amnesty for capital crimes in Chang'an, exempted the ward's residents from one year's rent, and bestowed silk on his staff according to rank.

sentences.zh: 又泰月稟過皇太子遠甚，諫議大夫褚遂良諫曰：「聖人尊嫡卑庶，謂之儲君，故用物不會，與王共之，庶子不得為比，所以塞嫌萌，杜禍源。

translations.literal: Moreover, Tai's monthly allowance far exceeded the crown prince's. Remonstrance Counselor Chu Suiliang remonstrated, saying: "The sage honors the primary wife and lowers the secondary; he is called the heir and stored lord. Therefore his goods do not tally with those of princes and are not shared with them—secondary sons may not be compared, thereby blocking the sprouting of suspicion and stopping the source of calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Tai's monthly allowance far exceeded the crown prince's. Remonstrance Counselor Chu Suiliang remonstrated: "The sage honors the primary heir and subordinates secondary sons. The crown prince's provisions must not match those of princes, nor may secondary sons be compared with him—this blocks suspicion and stops calamity at its source.

sentences.zh: 先王法制，本諸人情，知有國家者必有嫡庶，庶子雖愛，不得過嫡子。

translations.literal: The institutions of former kings rest on human feeling: those who know there is a state must have primary and secondary heirs; though a secondary son may be loved, he may not surpass the primary son.
translations.idiomatic: The institutions of former kings rest on human nature: every state has primary and secondary heirs; however beloved a secondary son may be, he must not surpass the primary heir.

sentences.zh: 如當親者疏，當尊者卑，則私恩害公，惑誌亂國。

translations.literal: If those who should be close are kept distant and those who should be honored are made low, then private affection harms the public good, confuses resolve, and disorders the state.
translations.idiomatic: If those who should be close are kept distant and those who should be honored are lowered, private affection harms the public good, confuses resolve, and disorders the state.

sentences.zh: 今魏王稟料過東宮，議者以為非是。

translations.literal: Now Prince of Wei's monthly provisions surpass the Eastern Palace's; commentators consider this wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Now Prince of Wei's allowance surpasses the Eastern Palace's, and commentators consider this improper.

sentences.zh: 昔漢竇太后愛梁王，封四十餘城。

translations.literal: Formerly in Han, Empress Dowager Dou loved the Prince of Liang and enfeoffed him with more than forty cities.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly in Han, Empress Dowager Dou loved the Prince of Liang and enfeoffed him with more than forty cities.

sentences.zh: 王築苑三百里，治宮室，為復道，費財巨萬，出警人蹕，一不得意，遂發病死。

translations.literal: The prince built a park three hundred li in extent, constructed palaces, made covered passages, spent wealth in the tens of thousands, went out with guards clearing the road—and because he was once displeased, he fell ill and died of rage.
translations.idiomatic: The prince built a park three hundred li across, constructed palaces and covered passages, spent vast sums, and went abroad with guards clearing the road—yet because he was once displeased, he fell ill and died of rage.

sentences.zh: 宣帝亦驕淮陽王，幾至於敗，輔以退讓之臣，乃克免。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan also indulged the Prince of Huaiyang, nearly to ruin; only with yielding and retiring ministers as assistants was disaster avoided.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan likewise indulged the Prince of Huaiyang, nearly to ruin; only with ministers who urged restraint was disaster avoided.

sentences.zh: 今魏王新出閤，且當示以節儉，自可在後月加歲增。

translations.literal: Now Prince of Wei has newly left the inner quarters; he should first be shown thrift, and increases may be added month by month and year by year thereafter.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Wei has only recently left the inner palace; he should first be taught thrift, with increases added month by month and year by year thereafter.

sentences.zh: 又宜擇師傅，教以謙儉，勉以文學，就成德器，此所謂聖人之教，不肅而成也。」

translations.literal: He should also choose tutors and teachers to instruct him in humility and thrift, encourage him in literary learning, and complete his moral capacity—this is what is called the sage's teaching, accomplished without severity."
translations.idiomatic: Tutors should be chosen to teach him humility and thrift, encourage his literary studies, and complete his moral character—this is the sage's teaching, accomplished without severity."

sentences.zh: 帝又敕泰入居武德殿，侍中魏徵亦言：「王為陛下愛子，欲安全之，則不當使居嫌疑之地。

translations.literal: The emperor also ordered Tai to move into Wude Hall. Palace Attendant Wei Zheng also said: "The prince is Your Majesty's beloved son; if you wish to keep him safe, you should not let him dwell in a place of suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also ordered Tai to move into Wude Hall. Palace Attendant Wei Zheng also said, "The prince is Your Majesty's beloved son; if you wish to keep him safe, you should not let him dwell in a place of suspicion.

sentences.zh: 今武德殿在東宮之西，昔海陵居之矣，論者為不可。

translations.literal: Now Wude Hall lies west of the Eastern Palace; formerly Prince of Hailing dwelt there, and commentators held it improper.
translations.idiomatic: Wude Hall lies west of the Eastern Palace; Prince of Hailing once dwelt there, and commentators held it improper.

sentences.zh: 雖時與事異，人之多言，尚或可畏。

translations.literal: Though times and affairs differ, the many words of men may still be feared.
translations.idiomatic: Though times and circumstances differ, the many words of men may still be feared.

sentences.zh: 又王之心亦弗遑舍，願罷之，成王以寵為懼之美。」

translations.literal: Moreover, in the prince's heart there is no leisure to set it aside; I wish it abolished, completing the prince's beauty of fearing favor as peril."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the prince's own heart cannot rest easy; I urge that this be revoked, completing the prince's virtue of fearing excessive favor."

sentences.zh: 帝悟，乃止。

translations.literal: The emperor understood and desisted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor understood and desisted.

sentences.zh: 時皇太子承乾病蹇，泰以計傾之，乃引駙馬都尉柴令武、房遺愛等布腹心，而韋挺、杜楚客相繼攝府事。

translations.literal: At that time Crown Prince Chengqian's feet were afflicted with lameness; Tai used stratagems to overturn him, and thus drew in Commandant of the Horse Guards Chai Lingwu, Fang Yiai, and others to spread his inner counsels, while Wei Ting and Du Chuke successively held acting charge of princely affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Crown Prince Chengqian was lame; Tai plotted to overturn him, drawing in Commandant of the Horse Guards Chai Lingwu, Fang Yiai, and others as confidants, while Wei Ting and Du Chuke successively managed his princely affairs.

sentences.zh: 二人者，為泰要結中朝臣，津介賂遺，群臣更附為朋黨。

translations.literal: These two men, for Tai's sake, bound together court ministers, served as go-betweens for bribes and gifts, and the various ministers in turn attached themselves as factional cliques.
translations.idiomatic: These two men bound court ministers to Tai's cause, serving as go-betweens for bribes and gifts until the ministers formed factions around him.

sentences.zh: 承乾懼，陰遣人稱泰府典簽詣玄武門上封，帝省之，書言泰罪，帝怒，即遣捕詰，不獲。

translations.literal: Chengqian was afraid and secretly sent a man posing as Tai's princely registrar to submit a sealed memorial at Xuanwu Gate. The emperor examined it; the writing listed Tai's crimes. The emperor was angry and immediately sent men to seize and interrogate, but they did not capture the man.
translations.idiomatic: Chengqian, in fear, secretly sent a man posing as Tai's registrar to submit a sealed memorial at Xuanwu Gate. The emperor read it—a list of Tai's crimes—and in anger sent men to seize the submitter, but they failed to capture him.

sentences.zh: 既而太子敗，帝陰許立泰，岑文本、劉洎請遂立泰為太子。

translations.literal: Before long the crown prince was defeated; the emperor secretly promised to establish Tai, and Cen Wende and Liu Ji requested that Tai immediately be made crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the crown prince fell; the emperor secretly promised to make Tai heir, and Cen Wende and Liu Ji urged that Tai be immediately installed as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 長孫無忌固欲立晉王，帝以太原石文有「治萬吉」，復欲從無忌。

translations.literal: Zhangsun Wuji firmly wished to establish Prince of Jin; the emperor, because stone inscriptions at Taiyuan bore the words "rule ten thousand, auspicious," again wished to follow Wuji.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangsun Wuji firmly wished to install Prince of Jin; the emperor, because stone inscriptions at Taiyuan bore the words "rule ten thousand, auspicious," again wished to follow Wuji.

sentences.zh: 泰微知之，因語晉王：「爾善元昌，得無及乎？」

translations.literal: Tai slightly knew of it and therefore said to Prince of Jin: "You are on good terms with Yuan-chang—will you not reach that far?"
translations.idiomatic: Tai learned of this and said to Prince of Jin, "You are on good terms with Yuan-chang—will you not go that far?"

sentences.zh: 王憂甚，帝怪之，以故對，帝憮然悟。

translations.literal: The prince was deeply troubled; the emperor wondered at it, and he answered with the reason; the emperor was startled into understanding.
translations.idiomatic: The prince was deeply troubled. When the emperor wondered at his distress and he explained the reason, the emperor was startled into understanding.

sentences.zh: 會召承乾譴勒，承乾曰：「臣貴為太子，尚何求？

translations.literal: It happened that Chengqian was summoned for reprimand and restraint. Chengqian said: "Your subject, honored as crown prince—what more does he seek?
translations.idiomatic: When Chengqian was summoned for reprimand, he said, "I was honored as crown prince—what more could I seek?

sentences.zh: 但為泰所圖，與朝臣謀自安爾。

translations.literal: Only because Tai plotted against me did I conspire with court ministers to secure my own safety.
translations.idiomatic: Only because Tai plotted against me did I conspire with court ministers to secure my own safety.

sentences.zh: 無狀之人，遂教臣為不軌事。

translations.literal: Worthless men thereupon taught your subject to do improper deeds.
translations.idiomatic: Worthless men thereupon led me into improper deeds.

sentences.zh: 若泰為太子，正使其得計耳。」

translations.literal: If Tai becomes crown prince, that would be exactly letting him succeed in his scheme."
translations.idiomatic: If Tai becomes crown prince, that would be exactly letting him succeed in his scheme."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「是也，有如立泰，則副君可詭求而得。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "It is so. If Tai were established, then the secondary lord could be sought by deceit and obtained.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "It is so. If Tai were established, the secondary heir could be obtained through intrigue.

sentences.zh: 使泰也立，承乾、治俱死；

translations.literal: If Tai were established, Chengqian and Zhi would both die;
translations.idiomatic: If Tai were established, Chengqian and Zhi would both die;

sentences.zh: 治也立，泰、承乾可無它。」

translations.literal: if Zhi were established, Tai and Chengqian could be without other harm."
translations.idiomatic: if Zhi were established, Tai and Chengqian could live without further harm."

sentences.zh: 即幽泰將作監，解雍州牧、相州都督、左武候大將軍，降王東萊。

translations.literal: He immediately confined Tai at the Directorate of Palace Construction, removed him as Governor of Yongzhou, Governor-General of Xiangzhou, and Grand General of the Left Martial Guard, and demoted him to Prince of Donglai.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately confined Tai at the Directorate of Palace Construction, stripped him of his posts as Governor of Yongzhou, Governor-General of Xiangzhou, and Grand General of the Left Martial Guard, and demoted him to Prince of Donglai.

sentences.zh: 因詔：「自今太子不道、籓王窺望者，兩棄之，著為令。」

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict stated: "From now on, if the crown prince is unprincipled or a feudal prince covets the throne, both shall be abandoned—let this be established as a statute."
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon an edict declared: "From now on, if the crown prince is unprincipled or a feudal prince covets the throne, both shall be abandoned—let this be established as law."

sentences.zh: 然帝猶謂無忌曰：「公勸我立雉奴，雉奴仁懦，得無為宗社憂，奈何？」

translations.literal: Yet the emperor still said to Wuji: "You urged me to establish Zhinvu. Zhinvu is benevolent and timid—will there not be worry for the altars of state? What is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: Yet the emperor still said to Wuji, "You urged me to establish Zhinvu. Zhinvu is benevolent but timid—will the altars of state not suffer? What is to be done?"

sentences.zh: 雉奴，高宗小字。

translations.literal: Zhinvu was Gaozong's childhood name.
translations.idiomatic: Zhinvu was Emperor Gaozong's childhood name.

sentences.zh: 泰尋改王順陽，居均州之鄖鄉。

translations.literal: Tai was soon changed to Prince of Shunyang and dwelt at Yunyang in Junzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Tai was soon made Prince of Shunyang and sent to dwell at Yunyang in Junzhou.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗持泰表語左右曰：「泰文辭可喜，豈非才士？

translations.literal: The emperor once held Tai's memorial and said to those about him: "Tai's literary style is pleasing—is he not a man of talent?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once held Tai's memorial and said to his attendants, "Tai's literary style is pleasing—is he not a man of talent?

sentences.zh: 我心念泰無已時，但為社稷計，遣居外，使兩相完也。」

translations.literal: My heart thinks of Tai without cease, but for the altars of state I send him to dwell abroad, so that both may be preserved whole."
translations.idiomatic: My heart never ceases to think of Tai, but for the sake of the realm I send him abroad so that both may be preserved."

sentences.zh: 二十一年進王濮。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was advanced to Prince of Pu.
translations.idiomatic: In 647 he was advanced to Prince of Pu.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，詔泰開府置僚屬，車服羞膳異等。

translations.literal: When Gaozong took the throne, an edict ordered Tai to open a princely residence and establish staff; carriage, robes, delicacies, and provisions were of a special grade.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong ascended the throne, an edict allowed Tai to open a princely residence with full staff; his carriage, robes, food, and provisions were of a special grade.

sentences.zh: 薨鄖鄉，年三十五，贈太尉、雍州牧。

translations.literal: He died at Yunyang at age thirty-five; posthumously given Grand Commandant and Governor of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died at Yunyang at age thirty-five and was posthumously appointed Grand Commandant and Governor of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 二子：欣、徽。

translations.literal: Two sons: Xin and Hui.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Xin and Hui.

sentences.zh: 欣嗣王，武后時為酷吏所陷，貶昭州別駕，薨。

translations.literal: Xin inherited the princely title; during Empress Wu's time he was trapped by a cruel official, demoted to vice-prefect of Zhaozhou, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Xin inherited the princely title; during Empress Wu's reign he was framed by a cruel official, demoted to vice-prefect of Zhaozhou, and died.

sentences.zh: 子嶠，神龍初得嗣王。

translations.literal: His son Qiao, at the beginning of Shenlong, was able to inherit the princely title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qiao, at the beginning of the Shenlong reign, was able to inherit the princely title.

sentences.zh: 開元中為國子祭酒，以罪貶鄧州別駕，薨。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan era he was Minister of the Directorate of Education; for an offense he was demoted to vice-prefect of Dengzhou and died.
translations.idiomatic: During Kaiyuan he served as Minister of the Directorate of Education; for an offense he was demoted to vice-prefect of Dengzhou and died.

sentences.zh: 徽封新安郡王。

translations.literal: Hui was enfeoffed as Prince of Xin'an commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was enfeoffed as Prince of Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 庶人祐字贊。

translations.literal: The Deposed Person You, styled Zan.
translations.idiomatic: The Deposed Prince Li You, whose courtesy name was Zan.

sentences.zh: 武德八年，王宜陽，進王楚，又王燕，已乃封齊，領齊州都督。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Wude he was made Prince of Yiyang, advanced to Prince of Chu, again Prince of Yan, and then enfeoffed as Prince of Qi, holding the post of Governor of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 625 he was made Prince of Yiyang, advanced to Prince of Chu, then Prince of Yan, and finally enfeoffed as Prince of Qi, serving as Governor of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 貞觀十一年始歸國。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Zhenguan he first returned to his domain.
translations.idiomatic: In 637 he first proceeded to his fief.

sentences.zh: 以明年入朝，以疾留京師。

translations.literal: The following year he came to court; on account of illness he remained in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he came to court; owing to illness he remained in the capital.

sentences.zh: 其舅尚乘直長陰弘智，憸人也，說祐曰：「王兄弟多，即上萬歲後，何以自全？

translations.literal: His maternal uncle Yin Hongzhi, Chief of the Imperial Carriage Office, was a crafty man and said to You: "Your Highness has many brothers; when His Majesty reaches his myriad years, how will you preserve yourself?
translations.idiomatic: His maternal uncle Yin Hongzhi, chief of the Imperial Carriage Office, was a crafty man who said to You, "Your Highness has many brothers; when the emperor passes away, how will you preserve yourself?

sentences.zh: 要須得士自助。」

translations.literal: You must obtain men to assist yourself."
translations.idiomatic: You must secure men to assist you."

sentences.zh: 乃引客燕弘亮謁祐，祐悅，賜金帛，使募劍客。

translations.literal: He thereupon introduced the guest Yan Hongliang to audience with You; You was pleased, granted gold and silk, and had him recruit swordsmen.
translations.idiomatic: He then introduced the adventurer Yan Hongliang to You, who was pleased, granted him gold and silk, and had him recruit swordsmen.

sentences.zh: 十五年還州。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he returned to his prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In 641 he returned to his prefecture.

sentences.zh: 初，帝用王府長史、司馬，必取骨鯁敢言者，有過失輒聞。

translations.literal: At first, when the emperor appointed princely Chief Administrators and Vice Administrators, he always chose men of firm backbone who dared speak; if there were faults they were immediately reported.
translations.idiomatic: At first, when appointing princely chief administrators and vice administrators, the emperor always chose men of firm principle who dared speak out; any fault was immediately reported.

sentences.zh: 而祐溺群小，好弋獵，長史薛大鼎屢諫不聽，帝以輔王無狀，免之，更用權萬紀。

translations.literal: But You drowned himself among petty men and loved archery and hunting; Chief Administrator Xue Dading repeatedly remonstrated without being heeded. The emperor, because he had assisted the prince without proper conduct, dismissed him and replaced him with Quan Wanji.
translations.idiomatic: But You surrounded himself with petty men and loved archery and hunting; Chief Administrator Xue Dading repeatedly remonstrated without being heeded. The emperor dismissed him for failing to guide the prince properly and replaced him with Quan Wanji.

sentences.zh: 萬紀性剛急，以法繩祐。

translations.literal: Wanji's nature was stern and urgent; he bound You with law.
translations.idiomatic: Wanji was stern and strict, restraining You with regulations.

sentences.zh: 有昝君謨、梁猛虎者，騎射得幸，萬紀斥之，祐私引與狎昵。

translations.literal: There were Zan Junmo and Liang Menghu, skilled in horsemanship and archery who gained favor; Wanji dismissed them, but You privately drew them in for intimate association.
translations.idiomatic: Zan Junmo and Liang Menghu, skilled in horsemanship and archery, had gained favor; Wanji dismissed them, but You privately drew them into intimate association.

sentences.zh: 帝數以書讓祐，萬紀恐並獲罪，即說祐曰：「王，上愛子，上欲王改悔，故數教責王。

translations.literal: The emperor repeatedly sent letters reproaching You; Wanji feared he would share in the guilt and thereupon said to You: "Your Highness is the emperor's beloved son; the emperor wishes Your Highness to reform and repent, and therefore repeatedly instructs and reproaches you.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor repeatedly sent letters reproaching You; Wanji, fearing he would share the blame, said to You, "Your Highness is the emperor's beloved son; the emperor wishes you to reform, and therefore repeatedly instructs and reproaches you.

sentences.zh: 誠能飭躬引咎，萬紀請入朝言之，上意宜解。」

translations.literal: If you can truly discipline your person and acknowledge fault, Wanji will request to go to court and speak of it; the emperor's mind should be relieved."
translations.idiomatic: If you can truly discipline yourself and acknowledge fault, I will go to court and speak on your behalf; the emperor's mind should be relieved."

sentences.zh: 祐因上書謝罪。

translations.literal: You thereupon submitted a letter apologizing for his fault.
translations.idiomatic: You thereupon submitted a letter of apology.

sentences.zh: 萬紀見帝，言祐且自新，帝悅，厚賜萬紀，而仍譙戒祐。

translations.literal: Wanji saw the emperor and said You was about to reform himself; the emperor was pleased, richly rewarded Wanji, and still admonished and warned You.
translations.idiomatic: Wanji saw the emperor and reported that You was about to reform; the emperor was pleased, richly rewarded Wanji, and still admonished You.

sentences.zh: 祐聞萬紀見勞，而己蒙責，以為賣己，益不平。

translations.literal: You heard that Wanji was rewarded for his audience while he himself had been reproached; he thought Wanji had sold him out and grew ever more resentful.
translations.idiomatic: You heard that Wanji was rewarded while he himself was reproached; believing Wanji had betrayed him, he grew ever more resentful.

sentences.zh: 會萬紀又以疑貳系君謨等，制祐不出國門，悉暴祐罪於朝，祐不勝忿。

translations.literal: It happened that Wanji again, on suspicion of disloyalty, imprisoned Junmo and the others, restrained You from leaving the state gates, and fully exposed You's crimes at court; You could not bear his anger.
translations.idiomatic: When Wanji again imprisoned Junmo and others on suspicion of disloyalty, confined You within the city gates, and fully exposed his crimes at court, You could bear his anger no longer.

sentences.zh: 有詔刑部尚書劉德威臨訊，頗實，帝召祐、萬紀還京師。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Minister of Justice Liu Dewei to conduct an on-site inquiry; the facts were largely confirmed, and the emperor summoned You and Wanji back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Minister of Justice Liu Dewei to conduct an on-site inquiry; the facts were largely confirmed, and the emperor summoned You and Wanji back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 祐與燕弘亮等謀，射殺萬紀，支解之。

translations.literal: You conspired with Yan Hongliang and others, shot and killed Wanji, and dismembered him.
translations.idiomatic: You conspired with Yan Hongliang and others, shot Wanji dead, and dismembered his body.

sentences.zh: 左右勸祐遂發兵，乃募城中男子年十五以上悉發，私署左右上柱國，光祿大夫，開府儀同三司，托東、托西等王，斥庫貲行賞，驅人築堞浚隍，繕甲兵。

translations.literal: Those about him urged You to raise troops forthwith; he then recruited all men in the city aged fifteen and above and mustered them all, privately appointing them Left Pillar of the State, Minister of Imperial Entertainments, Grandee of the State with privilege equal to the Three Excellencies, Princes Tuo-dong and Tuo-xi, and others; he expended treasury goods for rewards, drove men to build ramparts and dredge moats, and repaired armor and weapons.
translations.idiomatic: His followers urged him to raise troops; he recruited every man in the city aged fifteen or above, privately appointing them Pillar of the State, Minister of Imperial Entertainments, and Grandee of the State, naming some Princes Tuo-dong and Tuo-xi; he expended treasury goods for rewards, drove men to build ramparts and dredge moats, and repaired armor and weapons.

sentences.zh: 人惡之，皆夜縋亡去。

translations.literal: The people hated it; all by night let themselves down on ropes and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The people hated this; by night they let themselves down on ropes and fled.

sentences.zh: 詔兵部尚書李勣與劉德威發便道兵討之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Minister of War Li Jing together with Liu Dewei to dispatch troops by convenient routes to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Minister of War Li Jing and Liu Dewei to dispatch troops by rapid routes to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 祐日夜引弘亮等五人對其妃宴樂。

translations.literal: You day and night drew in Hongliang and five others to feast and make music with his consort.
translations.idiomatic: You day and night feasted and made music with Hongliang and five others in the presence of his consort.

sentences.zh: 語官軍，則弘亮妄言：「王毋憂，右手持酒啗，左手刀拂之。」

translations.literal: When they spoke of the government army, Hongliang spoke wildly: "Your Highness need not worry—hold wine in the right hand and drink, brush them aside with the sword in the left hand."
translations.idiomatic: When they spoke of the government army, Hongliang spoke wildly: "Your Highness need not worry—hold wine in the right hand and drink, brush them aside with the sword in the left hand."

sentences.zh: 祐信愛弘亮，聞之喜。

translations.literal: You trusted and loved Hongliang; hearing this he was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: You trusted and loved Hongliang; hearing this he was pleased.

sentences.zh: 帝手敕祐曰：「吾常戒汝勿近小人，正為此耳。

translations.literal: The emperor wrote a personal edict to You: "I have often warned you not to approach petty men—precisely for this reason.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wrote a personal edict to You: "I have often warned you not to approach petty men—precisely for this reason.

sentences.zh: 往吾子，今國仇，我上慚皇天，下愧后土。」

translations.literal: Formerly my son, now the state's enemy—I am ashamed before Heaven above and the earth below."
translations.idiomatic: Once my son, now the state's enemy—I am ashamed before Heaven above and the earth below."

sentences.zh: 題畢，涕而遣。

translations.literal: When he had finished writing, he wept and sent it.
translations.idiomatic: When he had finished writing, he wept and sent it.

sentences.zh: 祐檄諸縣，縣輒以聞。

translations.literal: You sent proclamations to the various counties; the counties immediately reported them.
translations.idiomatic: You sent proclamations to the surrounding counties; each county immediately reported them to the court.

sentences.zh: 祐窮蹙，上表曰：「臣，帝子也，為萬紀讒構，上天降靈，罪人斯得。

translations.literal: You, cornered, submitted a memorial saying: "Your subject, an emperor's son, was slandered and framed by Wanji; Heaven above sent down its spirit, and the guilty man has been obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Cornered, You submitted a memorial: "I, an emperor's son, was slandered and framed by Wanji; Heaven sent down its spirit, and the guilty man has been obtained.

sentences.zh: 臣狂失心，惝怳驚悸，左右無兵，即欲顛走，所以頗仗械以自衛護。」

translations.literal: Your subject, mad and having lost his mind, was distraught and startled with palpitations; with no troops at hand he wished at once to flee in disorder, and therefore somewhat relied on weapons to protect himself."
translations.idiomatic: I, mad and having lost my mind, was distraught and terrified; with no troops at hand I wished to flee, and therefore somewhat armed myself for self-protection."

sentences.zh: 時勣未至，而青、淄等州兵已集。

translations.literal: At that time Li Jing had not yet arrived, but troops from Qing, Zi, and other prefectures had already assembled.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jing had not yet arrived, but troops from Qing, Zi, and other prefectures had already assembled.

sentences.zh: 或勸祐虜子女走豆子為盜，計未決，兵曹杜行敏夜勒兵鑿垣入，祐與弘亮等閉門拒，至日中，行敏呼曰：「吾為國討賊，不速降，且焚。」

translations.literal: Some urged You to seize women and children and flee to Douzi to become bandits; the plan was not decided. Military Affairs Officer Du Xingmin by night led troops, breached the wall, and entered; You with Hongliang and others shut the gates to resist. By midday Xingmin called out: "I am suppressing rebels for the state—if you do not surrender quickly, I shall burn you."
translations.idiomatic: Some urged You to seize women and children and flee to Mount Douzi to become bandits; he had not decided when Military Affairs Officer Du Xingmin by night led troops through a breach in the wall. You and Hongliang shut the gates to resist. By midday Xingmin called out, "I am suppressing rebels for the state—surrender quickly or I shall burn you out."

sentences.zh: 士積薪，祐乃出，執送京師。

translations.literal: The soldiers piled firewood; You then came out and was seized and sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers piled firewood; You then came out and was seized and sent to the capital.

sentences.zh: 賜死內侍省，貶為庶人，葬以國公禮。

translations.literal: He was granted death at the Palace Domestic Service; demoted to commoner status; buried with the rites of a state duke.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted death at the Palace Domestic Service, demoted to commoner status, and buried with the rites due a state duke.

sentences.zh: 詔齊州給復一年，擢行敏巴州刺史，封南陽郡公。

translations.literal: An edict granted Qizhou one year's tax exemption; Xingmin was promoted to Prefect of Bazhou and enfeoffed as Duke of Nanyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted Qizhou one year's tax exemption; Xingmin was promoted to Prefect of Bazhou and enfeoffed as Duke of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 祐喜養鬥鴨，方未反，貍齚鴨四十餘，絕其頭去。

translations.literal: You loved raising fighting ducks; just before the rebellion, a raccoon-dog bit more than forty ducks and severed their heads.
translations.idiomatic: You loved raising fighting ducks; just before the rebellion, a raccoon dog killed more than forty of them, biting off their heads.

sentences.zh: 及敗，牽連誅死者凡四十餘人。

translations.literal: When he was defeated, those implicated and executed to death numbered more than forty in all.
translations.idiomatic: When he was defeated, more than forty persons implicated in the affair were executed.

sentences.zh: 祐之亂，州人羅石頭數祐罪，以刀直前刺祐，不克，殺之。

translations.literal: During You's rebellion, a man of the prefecture, Luo Shitou, enumerated You's crimes and advanced straight forward to stab You with a knife; he did not succeed and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: During You's rebellion, a man of the prefecture named Luo Shitou enumerated You's crimes and rushed forward to stab him; he failed and was killed.

sentences.zh: 詔贈亳州刺史。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously granted him Prefect of Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously appointed him Prefect of Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 祐嘗引騎徇邑聚，野人高君狀曰；

translations.literal: You once led horsemen to patrol the district settlements; a commoner named Gao Junzhuang said:
translations.idiomatic: You once led horsemen on patrol through the district settlements, when a commoner named Gao Junzhuang stepped forward and said:

sentences.zh: 「上親平寇難，土地甲兵不勝計。

translations.literal: "The late emperor personally pacified bandit troubles; land and armor and troops are beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: "The late emperor personally quelled rebellion and invasion; the empire's lands, armor, and troops are beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 今王以數千人為亂，猶一手搖泰山，又如君父何？」

translations.literal: Now Your Highness raises rebellion with several thousand men—it is like trying to shake Mount Tai with one hand. What then of your sovereign and father?"
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Highness would rebel with a few thousand men—it is like trying to shake Mount Tai with one hand. What will become of your sovereign and father?

sentences.zh: 祐擊禽之，愧其言，不能殺。

translations.literal: You struck and seized him; ashamed at his words, you could not kill him.
translations.idiomatic: You seized him by force, but ashamed at his words, you could not bring yourself to kill him.

sentences.zh: 詔擢榆社令。

translations.literal: An edict promoted him to Magistrate of Yushe.
translations.idiomatic: An edict promoted him to magistrate of Yushe.

sentences.zh: 蜀悼王愔，貞觀五年始王梁，與郯、漢、申、江、代五王同封。

translations.literal: Li Yin, Prince of Shu with posthumous title Daowang, was first enfeoffed as Prince of Liang in the fifth year of Zhenguan, receiving his title together with the five princes of Tan, Han, Shen, Jiang, and Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yin, posthumously titled Prince Daowang of Shu, was first enfeoffed as Prince of Liang in the fifth year of Zhenguan, receiving his title together with the five princes of Tan, Han, Shen, Jiang, and Dai.

sentences.zh: 徙王蜀，實封八百戶。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be Prince of Shu, with an actual fief of eight hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the title Prince of Shu, with a fief of eight hundred households.

sentences.zh: 出為岐州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out to serve as Prefect of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed prefect of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 數畋遊，為非法，帝頻責教，不悛，怒曰：「禽獸可擾於人，鐵石可為器，愔曾不如之！」

translations.literal: He repeatedly went hunting and violated the law; the emperor frequently rebuked and instructed him, but he did not reform. In anger the emperor said: "Wild beasts can be tamed by men, iron and stone can be made into vessels—Yin is not even their equal!"
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly went hunting and broke the law; the emperor often rebuked and admonished him, but he would not reform. The emperor said in anger, "Wild beasts can be tamed, iron and stone can be forged into vessels—Yin is not even their equal!"

sentences.zh: 乃削封戶及國官半，徙虢州。

translations.literal: Thereupon half his fief households and state officials were cut away, and he was transferred to Guozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon half his fief households and princely staff were stripped away, and he was transferred to Guozhou.

sentences.zh: 久之，還戶，增至千。

translations.literal: After a long while, the households were restored, increasing to one thousand.
translations.idiomatic: After some time his fief households were restored, and eventually increased to one thousand.

sentences.zh: 復出馳弋，敗民稼。

translations.literal: He again went out galloping on hunts, ruining the people's crops.
translations.idiomatic: He again went out hunting at full gallop, trampling the people's crops.

sentences.zh: 典軍楊道整叩馬諫，愔捽擊之。

translations.literal: Army Inspector Yang Daozheng seized the bridle and remonstrated; Yin grabbed and struck him.
translations.idiomatic: Army Inspector Yang Daozheng seized the bridle and remonstrated with him, but Yin grabbed and beat him.

sentences.zh: 御史大夫李乾祐劾愔罪，高宗怒，貶黃州刺史。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Li Qianyou impeached Yin for his crimes; Emperor Gaozong was angered and demoted him to Prefect of Huangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Li Qianyou impeached Yin for his offenses; Emperor Gaozong was enraged and demoted him to prefect of Huangzhou.

sentences.zh: 擢道整匡道府折沖都尉。

translations.literal: Daozheng was promoted to Defensive Commander of Kuangdao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Daozheng was promoted to Defensive Commander of Kuangdao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 吳王恪得罪，愔以母弟廢為庶人，徙巴州。

translations.literal: When Prince of Wu Ke fell from grace, Yin, as a younger maternal half-brother, was demoted to commoner status and transferred to Bazhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Wu Ke fell from grace, Yin—as his younger maternal half-brother—was demoted to commoner status and exiled to Bazhou.

sentences.zh: 俄封涪陵王，薨。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was enfeoffed as Prince of Fuling, then died.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was enfeoffed as Prince of Fuling, then died.

sentences.zh: 咸亨初，復爵士，贈益州大都督，陪葬昭陵，以子璠嗣王。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianheng, his princely rank was restored; he was posthumously granted Grand Governor-General of Yizhou and buried with honor at Zhaoling; his son Fan succeeded to the princedom.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Xianheng era, his princely rank was restored; he was posthumously made Grand Governor-General of Yizhou and granted burial at Zhaoling; his son Fan succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 璠，武后時謫死歸誠州。

translations.literal: Fan, under Empress Wu, was banished and died at Guicheng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Fan, under Empress Wu, was banished and died at Guicheng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，以朗陵王瑋子礻俞嗣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong, Langling Wang Wei's son Yi succeeded to the title.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Shenlong era, Yi, son of Prince Langling Wei, succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 越王貞，始王漢，後徙原，已乃封越。

translations.literal: Li Zhen, Prince of Yue, was first Prince of Han, later transferred to Yuan, and finally enfeoffed as Prince of Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhen, Prince of Yue, was first enfeoffed as Prince of Han, later transferred to Yuan, and finally given the title Prince of Yue.

sentences.zh: 貞善騎射，涉文史，有吏幹，為宗室材王。

translations.literal: Zhen was skilled at horsemanship and archery, versed in literature and history, possessed administrative ability, and was a talented prince among the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was skilled at horsemanship and archery, versed in literature and history, and possessed real administrative talent; among the imperial clan he was regarded as a prince of ability.

sentences.zh: 武后初，遷累太子太傅、豫州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Empress Wu's reign, he was promoted in succession to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and Prefect of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Empress Wu's reign, he rose in succession to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and prefect of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 中宗廢居房陵，貞乃與韓王元嘉及王子黃公譔，魯王靈夔、王子范陽王藹，霍王元軌、王子江都王緒，及子瑯邪王沖計議反正。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhongzong was deposed and confined at Fangling, Zhen then joined Prince of Han Yuanjia and his son Huang Gong Zhuan, Prince of Lu Lingqi and his son Prince of Fanyang Ai, Prince of Huo Yuan Gui and his son Prince of Jiangdu Xu, and his own son Prince of Langye Chong in plotting to restore the rightful order.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhongzong was deposed and confined at Fangling, Zhen joined Prince of Han Yuanjia and his son Huang Gong Zhuan, Prince of Lu Lingqi and his son Prince of Fanyang Ai, Prince of Huo Yuan Gui and his son Prince of Jiangdu Xu, and his own son Prince of Langye Chong in plotting to restore the rightful order.

sentences.zh: 垂拱四年，明堂成，悉追宗室行享禮，共疑後遂大誅戮不遺種，事且急，譔乃矯帝璽書賜沖曰：「朕幽縶，諸王宜即起兵。」

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chuigong, when the Bright Hall was completed, all members of the imperial clan were summoned to perform the sacrificial rites; together they suspected that afterward there would be a great slaughter leaving none alive. As the matter grew urgent, Zhuan forged an imperial seal edict and sent it to Chong, saying: "I am held in close confinement; the princes should immediately raise troops."
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Chuigong, when the Bright Hall was completed, all members of the imperial clan were summoned to perform the sacrificial rites. Together they feared that afterward Empress Wu would slaughter them to the last man.
