As matters grew urgent, Zhuan forged an imperial seal edict and sent it to Chong, saying, "I am held in close confinement; the princes should raise troops at once."

sentences.zh: 於是命長史蕭德琮募兵，告諸王師期。

translations.literal: Thereupon he ordered Chief Administrator Xiao Decong to recruit troops and inform the princes of the date for mobilization.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he ordered Chief Administrator Xiao Decong to recruit troops and notify the princes of the date for mobilization.

sentences.zh: 八月，沖先發，諸王莫有應者，獨貞將兵攻上蔡，破之，而沖已敗。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Chong rose first; none of the other princes responded. Only Zhen led troops to attack Shangcai, captured it, but Chong had already been defeated.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Chong rose first, but none of the other princes answered his call. Only Zhen led troops against Shangcai and took it—but by then Chong had already been defeated.

sentences.zh: 貞稍徇屬縣，得士七千，列五營：貞為中營，以裴守德為大將軍，領中營；

translations.literal: Zhen gradually subjugated the subordinate counties and gathered seven thousand men, arraying five camps: Zhen himself commanded the central camp, with Pei Shoude as Grand General leading the central camp;
translations.idiomatic: Zhen gradually brought the subordinate counties under his control and gathered seven thousand men, organizing them into five camps: Zhen himself commanded the central camp, with Pei Shoude as Grand General in charge of it;

sentences.zh: 趙成美為左中郎將，領左營；

translations.literal: Zhao Chengmei as Left Central Commandant, leading the left camp;
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Chengmei as Left Central Commandant, leading the left camp;

sentences.zh: 閭弘道為右中郎將，領右營；

translations.literal: Lu Hongdao as Right Central Commandant, leading the right camp;
translations.idiomatic: Lu Hongdao as Right Central Commandant, leading the right camp;

sentences.zh: 安摩訶為郎將，領後軍；

translations.literal: An Mohe as Commandant, leading the rear army;
translations.idiomatic: An Mohe as Commandant, leading the rear army;

sentences.zh: 王孝誌為右將軍，領前軍。

translations.literal: Wang Xiaozhi as Right General, leading the vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiaozhi as Right General, leading the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 以韋慶禮為司馬，署官五百。

translations.literal: Wei Qingli was made Chief Administrator, and five hundred officials were appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Qingli was appointed Chief Administrator, and five hundred officials were installed in office.

sentences.zh: 然肋誘無鬥志，家童皆佩符以辟兵。

translations.literal: Yet those coerced and enticed had no fighting spirit; household servants all wore talismans to ward off weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Yet those who had been coerced into service had no will to fight, and even household servants wore talismans to ward off weapons.

sentences.zh: 九月，後遣左豹韜衛大將軍曲崇裕、夏官尚書岑長倩率兵十萬討之，以鳳閣侍郎張光輔為諸軍節度，乃下詔削貞父子屬籍，改氏「虺」。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the empress dispatched Left Leopard-Taming Guard Grand General Qu Chongyu and Minister of Summer Affairs Cen Changqian to lead one hundred thousand troops against them, with Phoenix Pavilion Vice-Minister Zhang Guangfu as overall commander of the armies; an edict was then issued striking Zhen and his sons from the imperial register and changing their surname to "Hui."
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the empress dispatched Left Leopard-Taming Guard Grand General Qu Chongyu and Minister of Summer Affairs Cen Changqian with one hundred thousand troops to suppress them, appointing Phoenix Pavilion Vice-Minister Zhang Guangfu overall commander of the armies. An edict was then issued striking Zhen and his sons from the imperial register and changing their surname to Hui.

sentences.zh: 崇裕等次豫州，貞少子規及裴守德拒戰，兵潰，貞乃閉門守。

translations.literal: Chongyu and the others halted at Yuzhou; Zhen's youngest son Gui and Pei Shoude resisted in battle; the army collapsed, and Zhen then shut the gates and held the city.
translations.idiomatic: Chongyu and the others halted at Yuzhou. Zhen's youngest son Gui and Pei Shoude offered battle, but the army collapsed, and Zhen shut the gates and held the city.

sentences.zh: 守德者，驍勇士。

translations.literal: Shoude was a fierce and brave warrior.
translations.idiomatic: Shoude was a fierce and brave warrior.

sentences.zh: 貞始起，以女妻之，委以腹心。

translations.literal: When Zhen first rose in rebellion, he gave him his daughter in marriage and entrusted him with his innermost confidence.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhen first rose in rebellion, he gave Shoude his daughter in marriage and entrusted him with his innermost confidence.

sentences.zh: 至是，欲殺貞自贖。

translations.literal: At this point he wished to kill Zhen to redeem himself.
translations.idiomatic: At this point he wished to kill Zhen to redeem himself.

sentences.zh: 會軍薄城，家人白貞：「今事乃爾，王豈受戮辱者邪？」

translations.literal: Just as the army pressed close to the city, his family members told Zhen: "Things have come to this—would Your Highness submit to humiliation and execution?"
translations.idiomatic: Just as the army closed on the city, his family told Zhen, "Matters have come to this—would Your Highness submit to humiliation and execution?"

sentences.zh: 即仰藥死。

translations.literal: He immediately drank poison and died.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately drank poison and died.

sentences.zh: 規自殺，守德與主俱縊。

translations.literal: Gui killed himself; Shoude and the princess both hanged themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Gui killed himself; Shoude and the princess both hanged themselves.

sentences.zh: 起凡二十日敗。

translations.literal: From the rising to defeat, it was twenty days in all.
translations.idiomatic: From the rising to defeat, twenty days had passed.

sentences.zh: 始，貞臨水自鑒，不見其首，惡之，未幾及禍。

translations.literal: At the beginning, when Zhen looked at himself in the water, he could not see his head; he took this as an ill omen, and before long calamity befell him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Zhen looked at his reflection in the water, he could not see his head; he took this as an ill omen, and before long calamity befell him.

sentences.zh: 沖，貞長子也。

translations.literal: Chong was Zhen's eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: Chong was Zhen's eldest son.

sentences.zh: 好學，勇而才，累遷博州刺史。

translations.literal: He loved learning, was brave and talented, and was promoted in succession to Prefect of Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning, was brave and talented, and rose in succession to prefect of Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 初發，有士五千，度河趣武水，武水令告急魏州，州遣莘令馬玄素領兵先乘城，沖攻之，因風，積薪焚其門，火作風反，眾心沮解，其屬董元寂誦言：「王與國家戰，乃反爾。」

translations.literal: When he first rose, he had five thousand men; crossing the river he pressed toward Wushui. The magistrate of Wushui sent urgent word to Weizhou; the prefecture dispatched Magistrate of Shen Ma Xuansu to lead troops and seize the city first. Chong attacked it; relying on the wind, he piled firewood to burn the gate, but when the fire rose the wind reversed, spirits collapsed and the force dissolved. His follower Dong Yuanji recited aloud: "The prince fights the state, yet the fire turns against him."
translations.idiomatic: When he first rose, he had five thousand men. Crossing the river he pressed toward Wushui. The magistrate of Wushui sent urgent word to Weizhou, and the prefecture dispatched Magistrate of Shen Ma Xuansu to lead troops and seize the city first. Chong attacked it; relying on the wind, he piled firewood to burn the gate, but when the fire rose the wind reversed, morale collapsed, and the force dissolved. His follower Dong Yuanji cried aloud, "The prince fights the state, yet the fire turns against him."

sentences.zh: 沖斬以徇，眾懼，遂潰，唯家僮數十從之，乃走博州，為當關刺死。

translations.literal: Chong executed him as a warning; the men feared and fled. Only several dozen household servants followed him; he fled toward Bozhou and was stabbed to death at a checkpoint.
translations.idiomatic: Chong executed him as a warning; the men were terrified and fled. Only several dozen household servants followed him as he fled toward Bozhou, where he was stabbed to death at a checkpoint.

sentences.zh: 後命丘神勣討之，兵未至，沖已死，起七日敗。

translations.literal: Later Qiu Shenji was ordered to suppress him, but before the troops arrived Chong was already dead; from the rising to defeat, seven days had passed.
translations.idiomatic: Later Qiu Shenji was ordered to suppress him, but before the troops arrived Chong was already dead; from rising to defeat, seven days had passed.

sentences.zh: 二弟：茜、溫。

translations.literal: Two younger brothers: Xi and Wen.
translations.idiomatic: He had two younger brothers: Xi and Wen.

sentences.zh: 茜，常山公，坐死。

translations.literal: Xi, Duke of Changshan, was executed for his involvement.
translations.idiomatic: Xi, Duke of Changshan, was executed for his involvement.

sentences.zh: 溫以前告，流嶺南。

translations.literal: Wen, for having reported the plot in advance, was exiled to Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Wen, for having reported the plot in advance, was exiled to Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 初，貞騰檄壽州刺史趙瑰，諭以興兵且假道。

translations.literal: At the beginning Zhen sent a proclamation to Zhao Gui, Prefect of Shouzhou, explaining his intent to raise troops and requesting passage through his territory.
translations.idiomatic: At the outset Zhen sent a proclamation to Zhao Gui, prefect of Shouzhou, explaining his intent to raise troops and requesting passage through his territory.

sentences.zh: 瑰得檄，許為應，瑰妻常樂長公主亦趣諸王蚤立功，故瑰與主皆死。

translations.literal: When Gui received the proclamation he promised to respond; Gui's wife, Princess Changle of Chang, also urged the princes to achieve merit early—therefore both Gui and the princess were put to death.
translations.idiomatic: When Gui received the proclamation he promised to respond; his wife, Princess Changle of Chang, also urged the princes to act quickly and win merit—therefore both Gui and the princess were put to death.

sentences.zh: 濟州刺史薛顗與其弟紹謀應沖，率所部庸、調，治兵募士，沖敗，下獄死。

translations.literal: Xue Yan, Prefect of Jizhou, and his younger brother Shao plotted to respond to Chong; they led corvée labor and tax levies from their jurisdiction, drilled troops and recruited men. When Chong was defeated, Yan was imprisoned and died.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Yan, prefect of Jizhou, and his younger brother Shao plotted to answer Chong's call; they mobilized corvée labor and tax levies from their jurisdiction, drilled troops, and recruited men. When Chong was defeated, Yan was imprisoned and died.

sentences.zh: 顗，駙馬都尉瓘之子，母城陽長公主，封河東縣侯。

translations.literal: Yan was the son of Commandant-Consort Guan; his mother was Princess Chengyang the Greater; he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Hedong County.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was the son of Commandant-Consort Guan; his mother was Princess Chengyang the Greater; he had been enfeoffed as Marquis of Hedong County.

sentences.zh: 紹尚太平公主，擢累右玉鈐衛員外將軍，以主婿不加戮，餓死河南獄。

translations.literal: Shao was married to Princess Taiping; he was promoted in succession to Outside General of the Right Jade-Tally Guard. As the princess's son-in-law he was not executed, but starved to death in prison in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Shao was married to Princess Taiping and had risen in succession to Outside General of the Right Jade-Tally Guard. As the princess's son-in-law he was spared execution, but starved to death in prison in Henan.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，敬暉等奏沖父子死社稷，請復爵土，為武三思等沮罷。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong, Jing Hui and others memorialized that Chong and his father had died for the altars of state and requested restoration of their titles and fiefs; this was blocked and abandoned by Wu Sansi and others.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Shenlong era, Jing Hui and others memorialized that Chong and his father had died for the altars of state and requested restoration of their titles and fiefs, but Wu Sansi and others blocked the proposal.

sentences.zh: 開元四年，乃復爵土，有司謚死不忘君曰敬。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Kaiyuan their titles and fiefs were at last restored; the relevant offices gave the posthumous title Jing, meaning "dying without forgetting one's sovereign."
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Kaiyuan their titles and fiefs were at last restored; the relevant offices gave the posthumous title Jing—"dying without forgetting one's sovereign."

sentences.zh: 五年，又詔：「王嗣絕國除，朕甚悼焉。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, another edict stated: "The princely succession has been extinguished and the state line cut off; We are deeply grieved.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, another edict stated, "The princely line has been extinguished and the fief abolished; We are deeply grieved.

sentences.zh: 其以貞從孫故許王子夔國公琳嗣王，奉王祀。」

translations.literal: Let Zhen's collateral grandson Lin, State Duke of Kui, son of the late Prince of Xu's son, succeed to the princedom and maintain the prince's sacrifices."
translations.idiomatic: Let Zhen's collateral grandson Lin, State Duke of Kui, son of the late Prince of Xu's son, succeed to the princedom and maintain the prince's sacrifices."

sentences.zh: 琳薨，爵不傳。

translations.literal: When Lin died, the title was not transmitted.
translations.idiomatic: When Lin died, the title was not transmitted.

sentences.zh: 貞最幼息珍子謫嶺表，數世不能歸。

translations.literal: Zhen's youngest son Zhen; his son was banished to the lands south of the Ling Range, and for several generations they could not return.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen's youngest son Zhen—his son was banished to the far south, and for several generations the family could not return.

sentences.zh: 開成中，女孫持四世柩北還，求祔王塋。

translations.literal: During the Kaicheng era, a granddaughter brought back the coffins of four generations to the north and requested burial alongside the prince's tomb.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaicheng era, a granddaughter brought the coffins of four generations back north and requested burial alongside the prince's tomb.

sentences.zh: 詔嘉憫，敕宗正寺、京兆府為訪其兆，非陪陵者聽葬。

translations.literal: An edict praised and commiserated with her, ordering the Court of the Imperial Clan and the Capital Prefecture to search out a burial site; those not entitled to burial at the imperial tombs were permitted burial elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: An edict praised her devotion and commiserated with her plight, ordering the Court of the Imperial Clan and the Capital Prefecture to search out a burial site; those not entitled to burial at the imperial tombs were permitted burial elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 女名元真，為道士。

translations.literal: The woman's name was Yuanzhen; she was a Daoist priestess.
translations.idiomatic: The woman's name was Yuanzhen; she was a Daoist priestess.

sentences.zh: 紀王慎，始王申，後徙紀，食戶八百。

translations.literal: Li Shen, Prince of Ji, was first Prince of Shen, later transferred to Ji, with a fief of eight hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shen, Prince of Ji, was first enfeoffed as Prince of Shen, later transferred to Ji, with a fief of eight hundred households.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，遷襄州刺史，以治當最，天子璽書勞勉，人為立石頌德。

translations.literal: During Zhenguan he was transferred to Prefect of Xiangzhou; because his governance ranked highest, the Son of Heaven sent an imperial seal letter of commendation and encouragement, and the people erected a stone to praise his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenguan era he was appointed prefect of Xiangzhou; because his governance ranked highest, the emperor sent an imperial seal letter of commendation, and the people erected a stone monument praising his virtue.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，進戶至千。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, his fief households were increased to one thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year his fief households were increased to one thousand.

sentences.zh: 文明初，累遷太子太師、貝州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wenming he was promoted in succession to Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and Prefect of Beizhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Wenming era he rose in succession to Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and prefect of Beizhou.

sentences.zh: 慎少好學，善星步，與越王齊名，當世號「紀越」。

translations.literal: Shen from youth loved learning and was skilled at star-step calculations; he was equally famed with the Prince of Yue, and his contemporaries called them "Ji and Yue."
translations.idiomatic: From youth Shen loved learning and was skilled at astrology; he was equally famed with the Prince of Yue, and contemporaries called them "Ji and Yue."

sentences.zh: 初，貞連諸王起兵，慎知時未可，獨拒不與合。

translations.literal: At the beginning, when Zhen linked the princes in raising troops, Shen knew the time was not yet right and alone refused to join them.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhen linked the princes in raising troops, Shen knew the time was not yet right and alone refused to join them.

sentences.zh: 將就誅而免，改氏「虺」，載以檻車，謫巴州，薨於道。

translations.literal: He was about to be executed but was spared; his surname was changed to "Hui"; he was loaded into a caged cart, banished to Bazhou, and died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: He was about to be executed but was spared; his surname was changed to Hui; he was loaded into a caged cart, banished to Bazhou, and died on the road.

sentences.zh: 七子：續、琮、睿、秀、獻、欽、證。

translations.literal: Seven sons: Xu, Cong, Rui, Xiu, Xian, Qin, and Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: He had seven sons: Xu, Cong, Rui, Xiu, Xian, Qin, and Zheng.

sentences.zh: 續與秀最知名。

translations.literal: Xu and Xiu were the most renowned.
translations.idiomatic: Xu and Xiu were the most renowned.

sentences.zh: 續王東平，歷和州刺史，薨。

translations.literal: Xu was Prince of Dongping, served as Prefect of Hezhou, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Xu was Prince of Dongping, served as prefect of Hezhou, and died.

sentences.zh: 琮義陽王，睿楚國公，秀襄陽郡公，獻廣化郡公，欽建平郡公，五人並為武后所殺。

translations.literal: Cong was Prince of Yiyang, Rui Duke of Chu, Xiu Duke of Xiangyang, Xian Duke of Guanghua, Qin Duke of Jianping—the five were all killed by Empress Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Cong was Prince of Yiyang, Rui Duke of Chu, Xiu Duke of Xiangyang, Xian Duke of Guanghua, and Qin Duke of Jianping—all five were killed by Empress Wu.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，以證嗣王，擢左驍衛將軍，薨。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong, Zheng succeeded to the princedom, was promoted to General of the Left Martial Majestic Guard, and died.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Shenlong era, Zheng succeeded to the princedom, was promoted to General of the Left Martial Majestic Guard, and died.

sentences.zh: 子行同嗣。

translations.literal: His son Xingtong succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xingtong succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 琮三子：行遠、行芳、行休。

translations.literal: Cong's three sons: Xingyuan, Xingfang, and Xingxiu.
translations.idiomatic: Cong had three sons: Xingyuan, Xingfang, and Xingxiu.

sentences.zh: 始，琮與二弟同死桂林。

translations.literal: At the beginning, Cong and his two younger brothers died together at Guilin.
translations.idiomatic: Cong and his two younger brothers had died together at Guilin.

sentences.zh: 開元四年，行休請身迎柩，既至，無封樹，議者謂不可復得。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Kaiyuan, Xingxiu requested permission to go in person to receive the coffins; when he arrived, there were no marked trees, and those who discussed the matter said they could not be recovered.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Kaiyuan, Xingxiu requested permission to go in person to receive the coffins; when he arrived, there were no marked trees at the site, and onlookers said the remains could not be recovered.

sentences.zh: 行休歸，地布席以祈。

translations.literal: Xingxiu returned home, spread a mat on the ground, and prayed.
translations.idiomatic: Xingxiu returned home, spread a mat on the ground, and prayed.

sentences.zh: 是夜夢王乘舟，舟判為二。

translations.literal: That night he dreamed the prince riding in a boat, the boat split in two.
translations.idiomatic: That night he dreamed the prince riding in a boat that split in two.

sentences.zh: 既而適野，見東洲中斷，乃悟焉。

translations.literal: Then going out to the wilds, he saw the eastern islet cut in two, and understood.
translations.idiomatic: Then going out into the countryside, he saw the eastern islet cut in two—and understood.

sentences.zh: 又靈堂鎖一夕莖自屈，管上有指跡，一奇二並。

translations.literal: Moreover, at the spirit hall lock, overnight a stalk bent by itself; on the divining tube were fingermarks—one odd, two even.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, at the spirit hall lock overnight a stalk bent by itself; on the divining tube were fingermarks—one odd, two even.

sentences.zh: 使卜人筮之，曰：「屈，於文為屍出；

translations.literal: He had a diviner perform yarrow divination on it, who said: "Bent—in writing this signifies a corpse emerging;
translations.idiomatic: He had a diviner perform yarrow divination, who said, "Bent—in writing this signifies a corpse emerging;

sentences.zh: 指者，示也；

translations.literal: fingermarks signify showing;
translations.idiomatic: fingermarks signify showing the way;

sentences.zh: 一奇二並，三殯也。

translations.literal: one odd and two even—three coffins.
translations.idiomatic: one odd and two even—three coffins.

sentences.zh: 先王告之矣。」

translations.literal: The former prince has already told us."
translations.idiomatic: The former prince has already told us."

sentences.zh: 乃趣其所，發之如言，而一節獨闕。

translations.literal: He then hastened to that place and excavated as foretold, but one joint alone was missing.
translations.idiomatic: He then hastened to that place and excavated as foretold, but one joint of bone alone was missing.

sentences.zh: 行休號而寢，夢琮告曰：「在洛南洲。」

translations.literal: Xingxiu wailed and slept; he dreamed Cong telling him: "It is at Luonan Islet."
translations.idiomatic: Xingxiu wailed and slept; he dreamed Cong telling him, "It is at Luonan Islet."

sentences.zh: 明日，直殯南得之。

translations.literal: The next day, going straight south from the coffin, he found it.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, going straight south from the coffin, he found it.

sentences.zh: 於是以三喪歸，陪葬昭陵，贈琮陳州刺史。

translations.literal: Thereupon he brought the three coffins home; they were buried with honor at Zhaoling; Cong was posthumously granted Prefect of Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he brought the three coffins home; they were buried with honor at Zhaoling, and Cong was posthumously made prefect of Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 永昌時，行遠、行芳斥巂州，六道使至，行遠先就戮，行芳幼當赦，抱持請代，遂與俱死，西南人稱死悌云。

translations.literal: During Yongchang, Xingyuan and Xingfang were banished to Xizhou; when the Six-Circuit envoy arrived, Xingyuan was executed first; Xingfang, young, should have been pardoned, but he clung to his brother and begged to die in his place—thus both died together; the people of the southwest called this "dying in fraternal devotion."
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongchang era, Xingyuan and Xingfang were banished to Xizhou. When the Six-Circuit envoy arrived, Xingyuan was executed first; Xingfang, though young enough to be pardoned, clung to his brother and begged to die in his place—so both died together. The people of the southwest called this "dying in fraternal devotion."

sentences.zh: 慎女東光縣主，始八歲，聞慎有疾，不食，父哀之，紿雲已愈，主察顏色未平，終不肯禦，內外稱之。

translations.literal: Shen's daughter, Lady of Dongguang County, was only eight years old; hearing Shen was ill, she refused to eat. Her father pitied her and deceived her, saying he had recovered; the lady observed that his complexion was not yet restored and in the end would not take food. Inside and outside the household praised her.
translations.idiomatic: Shen's daughter, Lady of Dongguang County, was only eight years old. When she heard Shen was ill, she refused to eat. Her father pitied her and lied that he had recovered, but the girl saw that his complexion was not yet restored and would not take food. Inside and outside the household all praised her.

sentences.zh: 長適太子司議郎裴仲將。

translations.literal: When she came of age she was married to Palace Secretary of the Heir Apparent Pei Zhongjiang.
translations.idiomatic: When she came of age she was married to Palace Secretary of the Heir Apparent Pei Zhongjiang.

sentences.zh: 時妃、主多恃貴，以奢豫相矜，主獨儉素，姊弟誚曰：「人生富貴在得志，獨勤苦，欲何求？」

translations.literal: At the time consorts and princesses mostly relied on their exalted rank, competing in luxury and pleasure; the lady alone was frugal and plain. Her sisters and brothers mocked her, saying: "In life wealth and honor lie in fulfilling one's ambitions—alone you toil in hardship; what do you seek?"
translations.idiomatic: At the time consorts and princesses mostly relied on their exalted rank and vied in luxury and pleasure; the lady alone was frugal and plain. Her sisters and brothers mocked her, saying, "In life wealth and honor mean fulfilling one's ambitions—you alone toil in hardship; what do you seek?"

sentences.zh: 答曰：「我幼好禮，今行之不違，非得志謂何？

translations.literal: She answered: "From childhood I have loved ritual; now in practicing it I do not violate it—if this is not fulfilling one's ambitions, what is?
translations.idiomatic: She answered, "From childhood I have loved ritual; now in practicing it I do not violate it—if this is not fulfilling one's ambitions, what is?

sentences.zh: 且自古賢妃淑女以恭遜著名，驕縱敗德，況榮寵貴盛，儻來物也，可恃以淩人乎？」

translations.literal: Moreover, from antiquity worthy consorts and virtuous ladies have been famed for modesty and deference; arrogance and indulgence ruin virtue—how much more so when glory, favor, and exalted rank are things that come by chance; can one rely on them to look down upon others?"
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, from antiquity worthy consorts and virtuous ladies have been famed for modesty and deference, while arrogance and indulgence ruin virtue. Glory, favor, and exalted rank are things that come by chance—how can one rely on them to look down upon others?"

sentences.zh: 及王死，號慟，嘔血數升。

translations.literal: When the prince died, she wailed in grief and vomited several sheng of blood.
translations.idiomatic: When her father the prince died, she wailed in grief and vomited several pints of blood.

sentences.zh: 免喪，絕膏沐者二十年。

translations.literal: After the mourning period ended, she ceased using oils and cosmetics for twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: After the mourning period ended, she went twenty years without oils or cosmetics.

sentences.zh: 始，諸王、妃、主自垂拱後被害者皆槁掩之。

translations.literal: From the beginning, princes, consorts, and princesses who had been killed since the Chuigong era were all buried in dry, unmarked graves.
translations.idiomatic: From the beginning, princes, consorts, and princesses killed since the Chuigong era had all been buried in dry, unmarked graves.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，詔州縣普加求訪，祭以牲牢，復官爵，諸王皆陪葬昭、獻二陵。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong, an edict ordered the prefectures and counties to search for them everywhere, sacrifice to them with oxen and sheep, restore their ranks and titles, and all the princes were buried with honor at the Zhaoling and Xianling tombs.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Shenlong era, an edict ordered prefectures and counties to search for them everywhere, sacrifice to them with oxen and sheep, restore their ranks and titles, and all the princes were buried with honor at the Zhaoling and Xianling tombs.

sentences.zh: 主聞，感慟，卒，敕其子曰：「為我謝親戚，酷憤已雪，下見先王無恨矣！」

translations.literal: When the lady heard this, she was moved to grief and died. She instructed her son, saying: "Bid farewell to my relatives for me; the cruel injustice has been avenged, and going below to meet the former prince I shall have no regrets!"
translations.idiomatic: When the lady heard this, she was moved to grief and died. She instructed her son, saying, "Bid farewell to my relatives for me—the cruel injustice has been avenged, and when I go below to meet my father the prince I shall have no regrets!"

sentences.zh: 中宗為舉哀章善門，下詔褒揚。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhongzong held mourning for her at Zhangshan Gate and issued an edict praising her.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhongzong held mourning for her at Zhangshan Gate and issued an edict praising her virtue.

sentences.zh: 江殤王囂，封之明年薨，無後。

translations.literal: The Lamented Prince of Jiang, Xiao, died the year after his enfeoffment, leaving no heirs.
translations.idiomatic: The Lamented Prince of Jiang, Xiao, died the year after he was enfeoffed, leaving no heirs.

sentences.zh: 代王簡，已封薨，無後。

translations.literal: The Prince of Dai, Jian, died shortly after enfeoffment, leaving no heirs.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Dai, Jian, died shortly after receiving his title, leaving no heirs.

sentences.zh: 趙王福，貞觀十三年始王，出後隱太子。

translations.literal: The Prince of Zhao, Fu, was first enfeoffed in the thirteenth year of Zhenguan and was made the heir of the Hidden Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Zhao, Fu, was first enfeoffed in 639 and was made the heir of the Hidden Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 累遷梁州都督，實封八百戶。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Area Commander of Liangzhou, with a substantive fief of eight hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession to area commander of Liangzhou, with a substantive fief of eight hundred households.

sentences.zh: 薨，贈司空、并州都督，陪葬昭陵。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously granted Grand Minister of Works and Area Commander of Bingzhou, and was buried with honor at Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Grand Minister of Works and area commander of Bingzhou, and was buried with honor at Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 無子，神龍初，以蔣王惲孫思順嗣王。

translations.literal: Having no son, at the beginning of Shenlong the grandson of Prince of Jiang Yun, Sishun, succeeded to the princedom.
translations.idiomatic: Having no son, at the beginning of the Shenlong era the grandson of the Prince of Jiang, Yun—Sishun—succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 臯字子蘭，少補左司禦兵曹參軍。

translations.literal: Gao, styled Zilan, in youth was appointed Army Staff Officer of the Left Bureau of Imperial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Gao, whose courtesy name was Zilan, was in youth appointed army staff officer of the Left Bureau of the Imperial Guard.

sentences.zh: 天寶十一載嗣王。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Tianbao he succeeded to the princedom.
translations.idiomatic: In 752 he succeeded to the princedom.

sentences.zh: 事母太妃鄭以孝聞。

translations.literal: In serving his mother, Princess Dowager Zheng, he was famed for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: He was famed for filial devotion in serving his mother, Princess Dowager Zheng.

sentences.zh: 安祿山反，奉母逃民間，間走蜀，謁玄宗，由都水使者遷左領軍將軍。

translations.literal: When An Lushan rebelled, he escorted his mother and fled among the common people, making his way by hidden routes to Shu, where he had an audience with Emperor Xuanzong; from Commissioner of the Directorate of Waterways he was transferred to General of the Left Army Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rebelled, he escorted his mother and fled among the common people, making his way by hidden routes to Shu, where he had an audience with Emperor Xuanzong; from commissioner of the Directorate of Waterways he was transferred to general of the Left Army Guard.

sentences.zh: 上元初旱歉，臯祿不足養，請補外，不許，乃故抵輕法，貶溫州長史，俄攝州事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shangyuan, drought and famine struck; Gao's salary was insufficient to support his household. He requested an outside appointment but was not permitted, so he deliberately violated a minor law, was demoted to Chief Administrator of Wenzhou, and shortly assumed charge of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Shangyuan era, drought and famine struck, and Gao's salary was insufficient to support his household. He requested an outside appointment but was refused, so he deliberately violated a minor law, was demoted to chief administrator of Wenzhou, and shortly assumed charge of the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 州大饑，發官廩數十萬石賑餓者，僚史叩庭請先以聞，臯曰：「人日不再食且死，可俟命後發哉？

translations.literal: The prefecture suffered great famine. He released several hundred thousand shi from the official granaries to relieve the starving. The staff officials came to the court and begged that he report first to the throne. Gao said: "If people go a day without a second meal they will die—can grain be issued only after awaiting orders?
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture suffered great famine. He released several hundred thousand shi from the official granaries to relieve the starving. Staff officials came to the court and begged that he report first to the throne. Gao said, "If people go a day without a second meal they will die—can grain be issued only after awaiting orders?

sentences.zh: 茍殺我而活眾，其利大矣！」

translations.literal: If killing me can save the multitude, the benefit would be great!"
translations.idiomatic: If killing me can save the multitude, the benefit would be great!"

sentences.zh: 既貸，乃自劾，優詔開許，就進少府監。

translations.literal: After the grain was lent out, he impeached himself. A gracious edict absolved him, and he was promoted on the spot to Director of the Palace Workshops.
translations.idiomatic: After the grain was lent out, he impeached himself. A gracious edict absolved him, and he was promoted on the spot to director of the Palace Workshops.

sentences.zh: 時殿中侍御史李鈞與其弟京兆法曹參軍鍔宦既遂，不肯還鄉，母窮不自給。

translations.literal: At the time the Palace Censor Li Jun and his younger brother, Legal Administrator of the Capital District E, having achieved office through eunuch patronage, refused to return home; their mother was destitute and could not support herself.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the palace censor Li Jun and his younger brother, legal administrator of the capital district E, having achieved office through eunuch patronage, refused to return home; their mother was destitute and could not support herself.

sentences.zh: 臯行縣見之，嘆曰：「入則孝，出則悌，有餘力則學。

translations.literal: Gao, touring the counties, saw this and sighed, saying: "At home be filial, abroad be fraternal; when there is surplus strength, then study.
translations.idiomatic: While touring the counties Gao saw this and sighed, saying, "At home be filial, abroad be fraternal; when there is surplus strength, then study.

sentences.zh: 若二子者可與事君乎哉？」

translations.literal: Can men like these two be entrusted with serving a ruler?"
translations.idiomatic: Can men like these two be entrusted with serving a ruler?"

sentences.zh: 舉劾之，並錮死。

translations.literal: He impeached them both, and they were imprisoned and put to death.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached them both, and they were imprisoned and put to death.

sentences.zh: 召還，未得見，即上書言治道，詔授衡州刺史，為觀察使謾劾，貶潮州。

translations.literal: He was recalled but had not yet been granted an audience when he submitted a memorial on the way of governance. An edict appointed him Prefect of Hengzhou, but the observation commissioner falsely impeached him and he was demoted to Chaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled but had not yet been granted an audience when he submitted a memorial on the way of governance. An edict appointed him prefect of Hengzhou, but the observation commissioner falsely impeached him and he was demoted to Chaozhou.

sentences.zh: 會楊炎起道州為宰相，知臯直，復用為衡州刺史。

translations.literal: It happened that Yang Yan rose from Daozhou to become chancellor; knowing Gao's integrity, he restored him as Prefect of Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that Yang Yan rose from Daozhou to become chancellor; knowing Gao's integrity, he restored him as prefect of Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，御史覆訊，臯懼憂其母，出則囚服，入乃衣冠，貌言如平常。

translations.literal: At first, when censors re-examined the case, Gao feared distressing his mother; going out he wore convict's garb, but entering he put on cap and robes, his appearance and speech as usual.
translations.idiomatic: At first, when censors re-examined the case, Gao feared distressing his mother; going out he wore convict's garb, but entering he put on cap and robes, his appearance and speech unchanged.

sentences.zh: 及為潮，以遷入告。

translations.literal: When he was sent to Chaozhou, he told her only that he was being transferred inward.
translations.idiomatic: When he was sent to Chaozhou, he told her only that he was being transferred to a better post.

sentences.zh: 至是復位，乃言其實。

translations.literal: Now that he had regained his position, he told her the truth.
translations.idiomatic: Now that he had regained his position, he told her the truth.

sentences.zh: 建中元年，進拜湖南觀察使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianzhong he was promoted to Observation Commissioner of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: In 780 he was promoted to observation commissioner of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 前帥辛京杲貪虐，使部將王國良戍武岡，賴其富，即劾以死，國良恐，據縣反，斂荊、黔、洪、桂兵討之，再歲不能下。

translations.literal: The former commander Xin Jinggao was greedy and cruel; he had his subordinate general Wang Guoliang garrison Wugang and, coveting his wealth, impeached him on a capital charge. Guoliang feared for his life, seized the county and rebelled. Troops were gathered from Jing, Qian, Hong, and Gui to suppress him, but for two years they could not take him.
translations.idiomatic: The former commander Xin Jinggao was greedy and cruel; he had his subordinate general Wang Guoliang garrison Wugang and, coveting his wealth, impeached him on a capital charge. Guoliang feared for his life, seized the county and rebelled. Troops were gathered from Jing, Qian, Hong, and Gui to suppress him, but for two years they could not take him.

sentences.zh: 臯至，遺書曰：「觀將軍非敢大逆者，特逃讒抗死爾！

translations.literal: When Gao arrived, he sent a letter saying: "Observing the general, he is not one who dares great treason—he merely fled slander and resisted death!
translations.idiomatic: When Gao arrived, he sent a letter saying, "Observing the general, he is not one who dares great treason—he merely fled slander and resisted death!

sentences.zh: 將軍遇我，可以降，我固為京杲誣者，幸蒙雪，何忍以兵加將軍哉？

translations.literal: If the general meets with me, you may surrender. I myself was falsely accused by Jinggao and was fortunately cleared—how could I bear to bring troops against the general?
translations.idiomatic: If the general meets with me, you may surrender. I myself was falsely accused by Jinggao and was fortunately cleared—how could I bear to bring troops against you?

sentences.zh: 以為不然，我以陣術破將軍陣，以攻法屠將軍城，非將軍所度也。」

translations.literal: If you think otherwise, I shall break the general's battle line with formation tactics and storm the general's city with siege methods—not what the general expects."
translations.idiomatic: If you think otherwise, I shall break your battle line with formation tactics and storm your city with siege methods—not what you expect."

sentences.zh: 國良得書，喜且畏，因請降，然內尚首鼠。

translations.literal: When Guoliang received the letter he was both pleased and afraid, and therefore requested to surrender, yet inwardly he still wavered like a rat at both ends of a branch.
translations.idiomatic: When Guoliang received the letter he was both pleased and afraid, and therefore requested to surrender, yet inwardly he still wavered.

sentences.zh: 臯即日單騎稱使者造國良壘，賊延使者入，臯大呼其軍曰：「有識曹王者乎？

translations.literal: That same day Gao rode alone, claiming to be an envoy, and went to Guoliang's camp. The rebels invited the envoy in. Gao shouted to their army: "Is there anyone here who knows the Prince of Cao?
translations.idiomatic: That same day Gao rode alone, claiming to be an envoy, and went to Guoliang's camp. The rebels invited the envoy in. Gao shouted to their army, "Is there anyone here who knows the Prince of Cao?

sentences.zh: 乃我也。

translations.literal: It is I.
translations.idiomatic: It is I.

sentences.zh: 來受良降，良今安在？」

translations.literal: I have come to accept Liang's surrender—where is Liang now?"
translations.idiomatic: I have come to accept Liang's surrender—where is Liang now?"

sentences.zh: 一軍愕眙，不敢動，國良迎拜，叩頭請罪。

translations.literal: The whole army stared in astonishment and dared not move. Guoliang came forward to bow, kowtowed, and begged forgiveness.
translations.idiomatic: The whole army stared in astonishment and dared not move. Guoliang came forward to bow, kowtowed, and begged forgiveness.

sentences.zh: 臯執手，約為昆弟，則盡焚攻守具，散其兵。

translations.literal: Gao took his hand and pledged brotherhood with him, then burned all siege and defense equipment and dispersed the troops.
translations.idiomatic: Gao took his hand and pledged brotherhood with him, then burned all siege and defense equipment and dispersed the troops.

sentences.zh: 有詔赦之，賜名惟新。

translations.literal: An edict pardoned him and granted him the name Weixin.
translations.idiomatic: An edict pardoned him and granted him the name Weixin.

sentences.zh: 明年，持母喪至江陵。

translations.literal: The next year, bearing his mother's coffin, he reached Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, bearing his mother's coffin, he reached Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 會梁崇義反，奪為左衛大將軍，復觀察湖南。

translations.literal: It happened that Liang Chongyi rebelled; Gao was stripped of mourning duty and appointed Grand General of the Left Guard, again observing Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that Liang Chongyi rebelled; Gao was stripped of mourning duty and appointed grand general of the Left Guard, again serving as observation commissioner of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 李希烈反，遷江西節度使。

translations.literal: When Li Xilie rebelled, Gao was transferred to Military Commissioner of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Xilie rebelled, Gao was transferred to military commissioner of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 受命日，不宿家，至豫章，大令將吏曰：「有功未申與懷器謀不發者，皆自言。」

translations.literal: On the day he received his commission he did not stay at home; reaching Yuzhang, he issued a great order to officers and clerks, saying: "Those with unreported merit and those who harbored weapons but did not launch their plots—speak for yourselves."
translations.idiomatic: On the day he received his commission he did not stay at home; reaching Yuzhang, he issued a great order to officers and clerks, saying, "Those with unreported merit and those who harbored weapons but did not launch their plots—speak for yourselves."

sentences.zh: 得裨校伊慎、李伯潛、劉旻，悉補大將。

translations.literal: He found staff officers Yi Shen, Li Boqian, and Liu Min, and all were appointed major generals.
translations.idiomatic: He found staff officers Yi Shen, Li Boqian, and Liu Min, and all were appointed major generals.

sentences.zh: 擢王鍔為中軍，以馬彜、許孟容為幕府。

translations.literal: He promoted Wang E to command the center army and made Ma Yi and Xu Mengrong his staff.
translations.idiomatic: He promoted Wang E to command the center army and made Ma Yi and Xu Mengrong members of his staff.

sentences.zh: 治戰艦，裒兵二萬，以士二千五百委慎等教之。

translations.literal: He built war vessels and gathered twenty thousand troops, assigning two thousand five hundred soldiers to Shen and the others to train them.
translations.idiomatic: He built war vessels and gathered twenty thousand troops, assigning two thousand five hundred soldiers to Shen and the others to train them.

sentences.zh: 自將五百人，教以秦兵團力法，聯其賞罰，弛張如一，乃約以五百人擊慎卒二千五百，莫能當其鋒，即盡以教之。

translations.literal: He personally led five hundred men and taught them the Qin army's group-strength method, linking their rewards and punishments so that advance and withdrawal were as one; then he arranged for the five hundred to attack Shen's two thousand five hundred, and none could withstand their charge—so he had them all taught the method.
translations.idiomatic: He personally led five hundred men and taught them the Qin army's group-strength method, linking their rewards and punishments so that advance and withdrawal moved as one; then he arranged for the five hundred to attack Shen's two thousand five hundred, and none could withstand their charge—so he had the whole force taught the method.

sentences.zh: 初，慎嘗從希烈平襄州，至是，希烈懼為臯用，即反間，德宗信之，將誅慎，臯請赦之，使自效。

translations.literal: At first Shen had followed Xilie in pacifying Xiangzhou; now Xilie feared Gao would employ him and spread disinformation. Dezong believed it and was about to execute Shen. Gao requested a pardon and had him prove himself.
translations.idiomatic: Shen had once followed Xilie in pacifying Xiangzhou; now Xilie feared Gao would employ him and spread disinformation. Dezong believed it and was about to execute Shen. Gao requested a pardon and had him prove himself.

sentences.zh: 會與賊夾江陣，臯勉慎立功，以所乘馬及其鎧賜之，使將先鋒，斬賊數百級，乃免。

translations.literal: It happened that they faced the rebels in battle lines on opposite banks of the river. Gao urged Shen to earn merit, bestowed on him the horse he himself rode and his armor, and had him lead the vanguard; he beheaded several hundred of the enemy, and only then was Shen spared.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that they faced the rebels in battle lines on opposite banks of the river. Gao urged Shen to earn merit, bestowed on him the horse he himself rode and his armor, and had him lead the vanguard; he beheaded several hundred of the enemy, and only then was Shen spared.

sentences.zh: 賊柵蔡山不可攻，臯聲言西取蘄，引兵艦循崖溯江上。

translations.literal: The rebels' fort at Cai Mountain could not be attacked. Gao declared he would take Qi to the west and led his warships along the cliffs upstream on the river.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels' fort at Cai Mountain could not be taken by assault. Gao declared he would take Qi to the west and led his warships along the cliffs upstream on the river.

sentences.zh: 賊聞，以羸師保柵，悉軍行江北，與臯直。

translations.literal: When the rebels heard this, they left a weak force to hold the fort and moved their whole army along the north bank of the river, parallel with Gao.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels heard this, they left a weak force to hold the fort and moved their whole army along the north bank of the river, parallel with Gao.

sentences.zh: 西去蔡山三百里，臯遣步士悉登舟，順流下，攻蔡山，拔之。

translations.literal: Three hundred li west of Cai Mountain, Gao had his infantry all board the ships, drift downstream, attack Cai Mountain, and capture it.
translations.idiomatic: Three hundred li west of Cai Mountain, Gao had his infantry all board the ships, drift downstream, attack Cai Mountain, and capture it.

sentences.zh: 間一日，賊救至，遂大敗，乃取蘄州，降其將李良，平黃州，兵益振。

translations.literal: One day later the rebel relief arrived and suffered a great defeat. He then took Qizhou, accepted the surrender of their general Li Liang, pacified Huangzhou, and his army's morale grew ever stronger.
translations.idiomatic: One day later the rebel relief arrived and suffered a great defeat. He then took Qizhou, accepted the surrender of their general Li Liang, pacified Huangzhou, and his army's morale grew ever stronger.

sentences.zh: 會舒王為元帥，授臯前軍兵馬使。

translations.literal: It happened that the Prince of Shu was made commander-in-chief; Gao was appointed Army and Horse Commissioner of the vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that the Prince of Shu was made commander-in-chief; Gao was appointed army and horse commissioner of the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 俄而天子狩奉天，鹽鐵使包佶為陳少遊所窘，以運艚溯江，次蘄口，希烈使杜少誠將步騎三萬將絕江道，臯遣伊慎兵七千禦於永安，走之。

translations.literal: Shortly the Son of Heaven went on campaign to Fengtian. The Salt and Iron Commissioner Bao Ji, pressed by Chen Shaoyou, was transporting grain barges upstream and halted at Qikou. Xilie sent Du Shaocheng with thirty thousand infantry and cavalry to cut the river route. Gao dispatched Yi Shen with seven thousand troops to resist at Yong'an and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly the emperor went on campaign to Fengtian. The salt and iron commissioner Bao Ji, pressed by Chen Shaoyou, was transporting grain barges upstream and halted at Qikou. Xilie sent Du Shaocheng with thirty thousand infantry and cavalry to cut the river route. Gao dispatched Yi Shen with seven thousand troops to resist at Yong'an and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 以功進工部尚書。

translations.literal: For his merit he was promoted to Minister of the Works.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was promoted to minister of the Works.

sentences.zh: 帝駐梁州，臯之貢助相望。

translations.literal: The emperor stayed at Liangzhou; Gao's tribute and aid arrived in unbroken succession.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor stayed at Liangzhou; Gao's tribute and aid arrived in unbroken succession.

sentences.zh: 以天子處外，乃不敢居城府，出屯西塞山大洲，徙郡縣為軍市。

translations.literal: Because the Son of Heaven was abroad, he dared not dwell in the walled city and prefectural seat, but went out to encamp on the great islet of Xisai Mountain and moved the prefecture and counties into a military market.
translations.idiomatic: Because the emperor was abroad, he dared not dwell in the walled city and prefectural seat, but went out to encamp on the great islet of Xisai Mountain and moved the prefecture and counties into a military market.

sentences.zh: 改戶部尚書。

translations.literal: He was changed to Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was changed to minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 又遣伊慎、王鍔攻安州，未下，希烈遣劉戒虛以步騎八千援之，臯命李伯潛迎擊於應山，俘之，遂下安州，斬偽刺史王嘉祥。

translations.literal: He again sent Yi Shen and Wang E to attack Anzhou, but it was not taken. Xilie dispatched Liu Jie Xu with eight thousand infantry and cavalry to relieve it. Gao ordered Li Boqian to meet and strike them at Yingshan, captured them, then took Anzhou and beheaded the false prefect Wang Jiaxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He again sent Yi Shen and Wang E to attack Anzhou, but it was not taken. Xilie dispatched Liu Jie Xu with eight thousand infantry and cavalry to relieve it. Gao ordered Li Boqian to meet and strike them at Yingshan, captured them, then took Anzhou and beheaded the false prefect Wang Jiaxiang.

sentences.zh: 希烈別遣兵援隋州，臯破之厲鄉，因下平靜、白雁關，賊遂不敢南略。

translations.literal: Xilie separately sent troops to relieve Suizhou; Gao defeated them at Lixiang, then took Pingjing and Baiyan Pass, and the rebels thereafter dared not march south in aggression.
translations.idiomatic: Xilie separately sent troops to relieve Suizhou; Gao defeated them at Lixiang, then took Pingjing and Baiyan Pass, and the rebels thereafter dared not march south in aggression.

sentences.zh: 遷荊南節度使，賜實封三百戶。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Military Commissioner of Jingnan and granted a substantive fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to military commissioner of Jingnan and granted a substantive fief of three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 凡戰大小三十二，取州五、縣二十，斬首三萬三千，禽生萬六千，未嘗敗。

translations.literal: In all he fought thirty-two engagements, great and small; took five prefectures and twenty counties; beheaded thirty-three thousand; captured sixteen thousand alive—and never suffered defeat.
translations.idiomatic: In all he fought thirty-two engagements, great and small; took five prefectures and twenty counties; beheaded thirty-three thousand; captured sixteen thousand alive—and never suffered defeat.

sentences.zh: 師所過，不敢伐桑棗、踐禾稼。

translations.literal: Where his army passed, they did not dare cut mulberry or jujube trees or trample the grain in the fields.
translations.idiomatic: Where his army passed, they did not dare cut mulberry or jujube trees or trample the grain in the fields.

sentences.zh: 朝廷仰食江淮，而西道出九江，至大別，皆與賊接，臯轉戰數千里，餉路遂通，江漢倚臯為固。

translations.literal: The court relied on the Jianghuai region for food, yet the western route from Jiujiang to Dabie all bordered rebel territory. Gao fought over several thousand li, the supply routes were opened, and the Jianghan region relied on Gao as its bulwark.
translations.idiomatic: The court relied on the Jianghuai region for food, yet the western route from Jiujiang to Dabie all bordered rebel territory. Gao fought over several thousand li, the supply routes were opened, and the Jianghan region relied on Gao as its bulwark.

sentences.zh: 淮西平，乃請護喪歸東都，帝走中人赗吊。

translations.literal: When Huai West was pacified, he requested leave to escort his mother's coffin home to the Eastern Capital; the emperor sent palace envoys with funeral gifts and condolences.
translations.idiomatic: When Huai West was pacified, he requested leave to escort his mother's coffin home to the Eastern Capital; the emperor sent palace envoys with funeral gifts and condolences.

sentences.zh: 訖葬來朝，還就鎮。

translations.literal: When the burial was finished he came to court, then returned to his command.
translations.idiomatic: When the burial was finished he came to court, then returned to his command.

sentences.zh: 初，江陵東北傍漢有古鄣，不治，歲輒溢。

translations.literal: At first, northeast of Jiangling along the Han River there was an ancient dike that was not maintained, and every year it overflowed.
translations.idiomatic: At first, northeast of Jiangling along the Han River there was an ancient dike that was not maintained, and every year it overflowed.

sentences.zh: 臯修塞之，得其下良田五千頃。

translations.literal: Gao repaired and blocked it, gaining five thousand qing of fine fields below.
translations.idiomatic: Gao repaired and blocked it, gaining five thousand qing of fine fields below.

sentences.zh: 規江南廢洲為廬舍，構二橋跨江，而流人自占者二千餘家。

translations.literal: He planned abandoned islets south of the river as dwelling sites, built two bridges spanning the river, and more than two thousand refugee households settled there on their own.
translations.idiomatic: He planned abandoned islets south of the river as dwelling sites, built two bridges spanning the river, and more than two thousand refugee households settled there on their own.

sentences.zh: 繇荊抵樂鄉二百里，其間墟聚凡數十，不井飲，臯始命鑿井以便人。

translations.literal: From Jing to Lexiang was two hundred li; between them were several dozen hamlets that had no well water. Gao first ordered wells dug to benefit the people.
translations.idiomatic: From Jing to Lexiang was two hundred li; between them were several dozen hamlets that had no well water. Gao first ordered wells dug to benefit the people.

sentences.zh: 貞元初，吳少誠擅蔡，故徙臯鎮山南東道，割隋、汝以益軍，練兵峙糧，市回鶻馬以益戰騎，歲時大畋以教士，少誠畏之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenyuan, Wu Shaochéng held Cai by force, so Gao was transferred to command Shannan East Circuit; Sui and Ru were carved off to augment his army. He trained troops and stockpiled grain, purchased Uyghur horses to increase his cavalry, and held great hunts each year to drill his men—Shaochéng feared him.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhenyuan era, Wu Shaochéng held Cai by force, so Gao was transferred to command Shannan East Circuit; Sui and Ru were carved off to augment his army. He trained troops and stockpiled grain, purchased Uyghur horses to increase his cavalry, and held great hunts each year to drill his men—Shaochéng feared him.

sentences.zh: 臯性勤儉，能知人疾苦。

translations.literal: Gao by nature was diligent and frugal, and could understand people's hardships.
translations.idiomatic: Gao was by nature diligent and frugal, and understood people's hardships.

sentences.zh: 參聽微隱，盡得吏下短長，其賞罰必信。

translations.literal: He attended to subtle and hidden matters, fully grasping the strengths and failings of those below him; his rewards and punishments were always trustworthy.
translations.idiomatic: He attended to subtle and hidden matters, fully grasping the strengths and failings of those below him; his rewards and punishments were always trustworthy.

sentences.zh: 所至常平物估，豪舉不得擅其利。

translations.literal: Wherever he went he stabilized market prices, and powerful speculators could not monopolize profit.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he went he stabilized market prices, and powerful speculators could not monopolize profit.

sentences.zh: 教為戰艦，挾二輪蹈之，鼓水疾進，駛於陣馬。

translations.literal: He had war vessels built with two wheels that men trod, beating the water to advance swiftly—faster than cavalry in battle formation.
translations.idiomatic: He had war vessels built with two wheels that men trod, beating the water to advance swiftly—faster than cavalry in battle formation.

sentences.zh: 有所造作，皆用省而利長。

translations.literal: Whatever he made or built used less material yet yielded greater benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever he made or built used less material yet yielded greater benefit.

sentences.zh: 以物遺人，必自視衡量，庫帛皆印署，以杜吏謾。

translations.literal: When he gave goods to others he always measured them himself; all cloth in the storehouse was stamped and signed to prevent clerks' deceit.
translations.idiomatic: When he gave goods to others he always measured them himself; all cloth in the storehouse was stamped and signed to prevent clerks' deceit.

sentences.zh: 扶鳳馬彜未知名，臯識之，卒以正直稱。

translations.literal: Ma Yi of Fufeng was not yet known by name; Gao recognized his talent, and in the end he was famed for integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Yi of Fufeng was not yet known by name; Gao recognized his talent, and in the end he was famed for integrity.

sentences.zh: 張柬之有園圃在襄陽，臯嘗宴集，將市取之。

translations.literal: Zhang Jianzhi had a garden estate at Xiangyang; Gao once held a banquet there and was about to purchase it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jianzhi had a garden estate at Xiangyang; Gao once held a banquet there and was about to purchase it.

sentences.zh: 彜曰：「漢陽有中興功，今遺業當百世共保，奈何使其子孫鬻乎？」

translations.literal: Ma Yi said: "Hanyang has merit in restoring the dynasty; this legacy ought to be preserved by all for a hundred generations—how can we let his descendants sell it?"
translations.idiomatic: Ma Yi said, "Hanyang has merit in restoring the dynasty; this legacy ought to be preserved by all for a hundred generations—how can we let his descendants sell it?"

sentences.zh: 臯謝曰：「主吏失詞，以為君羞，微君安得聞此言？」

translations.literal: Gao apologized, saying: "My chief clerk misspoke and shamed you before your guest—without you, how would I have heard these words?"
translations.idiomatic: Gao apologized, saying, "My chief clerk misspoke and shamed you before your guest—without you, how would I have heard these words?"

sentences.zh: 卒年六十，贈尚書右僕射，謚曰成。

translations.literal: He died at sixty years of age, was posthumously granted Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, and was given the posthumous title Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty years of age, was posthumously made right vice director of the Imperial Secretariat, and was given the posthumous title Cheng.

sentences.zh: 臯嘗自創意為欹器，以飖木上出五觚，下銳圓，為盂形，所容二豆，少則水弱，多則強，中則水器力均，雖動搖，乃不覆云。

translations.literal: Gao once devised of his own invention a tipping vessel: using floating wood, the upper part had five angular sides, the lower part was sharp and round, shaped like a bowl, holding two dou; with too little water it leaned weakly, with too much it leaned strongly, but at the middle the water and vessel balanced in force—even when shaken, it would not overturn, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Gao once devised of his own invention a tipping vessel: using floating wood, the upper part had five angular sides, the lower part was sharp and round, shaped like a bowl, holding two dou; with too little water it leaned weakly, with too much it leaned strongly, but at the middle the water and vessel balanced in force—even when shaken, it would not overturn, it is said.

sentences.zh: 子象古、道古。

translations.literal: His sons were Xianggu and Daogu.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Xianggu and Daogu.

sentences.zh: 象古，元和中，自衡州刺史擢安南都護，貪縱不法。

translations.literal: Xianggu, during Yuanhe, was promoted from Prefect of Hengzhou to Protector-General of Annan; he was greedy, indulgent, and lawless.
translations.idiomatic: Xianggu, during the Yuanhe era, was promoted from prefect of Hengzhou to protector-general of Annan; he was greedy, indulgent, and lawless.

sentences.zh: 驩州刺史楊清者，蠻酋也，象古忌其豪，召為牙門將，常郁郁思亂。

translations.literal: The Prefect of Huanzhou, Yang Qing, was a tribal chieftain. Xianggu envied his power and summoned him to serve as garrison gate general; he was often depressed and brooded on rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect of Huanzhou, Yang Qing, was a tribal chieftain. Xianggu envied his power and summoned him to serve as garrison gate general; he was often depressed and brooded on rebellion.

sentences.zh: 會討黃賊，象古發甲助之，乃授清兵三千。

translations.literal: It happened that they were campaigning against the Yellow Bandits; Xianggu dispatched armor and troops to assist, and thereby entrusted Qing with three thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that they were campaigning against the Yellow Bandits; Xianggu dispatched armor and troops to assist, and thereby entrusted Qing with three thousand men.

sentences.zh: 清與子誌烈還襲安南，殺象古並其家。

translations.literal: Qing, with his son Zhilie, turned back and raided Annan, killing Xianggu and his whole household.
translations.idiomatic: Qing, with his son Zhilie, turned back and raided Annan, killing Xianggu and his whole household.

sentences.zh: 詔赦清為瓊州刺史，以桂仲武為都護。

translations.literal: An edict pardoned Qing and appointed him Prefect of Qiongzhou; Gui Zhongwu was made Protector-General.
translations.idiomatic: An edict pardoned Qing and appointed him prefect of Qiongzhou; Gui Zhongwu was made protector-general.

sentences.zh: 清拒命，仲武分諭渠酋，兵皆附，破城，斬清，夷其族。

translations.literal: Qing refused the order. Zhongwu sent envoys separately to persuade the tribal chiefs; their troops all attached to him. He stormed the city, beheaded Qing, and exterminated his clan.
translations.idiomatic: Qing refused the order. Zhongwu sent envoys separately to persuade the tribal chiefs; their troops all attached to him. He stormed the city, beheaded Qing, and exterminated his clan.

sentences.zh: 道古，舉進士，獻書闕下，擢校書郎、集賢院學士。

translations.literal: Daogu passed the jinshi examination, presented a book at the palace gates, and was promoted to Collator and Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Daogu passed the jinshi examination, presented a book at the palace gates, and was promoted to collator and academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 累遷司門員外郎，歷利、隋、唐、睦四州刺史。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice Gate, and served as prefect of Li, Sui, Tang, and Mu—four prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession to vice director of the Ministry of Justice Gate, and served as prefect of Li, Sui, Tang, and Mu—four prefectures.

sentences.zh: 柳公綽鎮鄂嶽，為飛譖上聞，憲宗欲代之。

translations.literal: When Liu Gongchuo commanded E and Yue, slander reached the throne by secret report; Emperor Xianzong wished to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Gongchuo commanded E and Yue, slander reached the throne by secret report; Emperor Xianzong wished to replace him.

sentences.zh: 裴度言：「嗣曹王臯嘗能以江漢兵制李希烈，威惠在人，今以其子將，必有功。」

translations.literal: Pei Du said: "The heir Prince of Cao, Gao, was once able to restrain Li Xilie with Jianghan troops; his authority and kindness live in men's hearts. Now, sending his son to command, there will surely be merit."
translations.idiomatic: Pei Du said, "The heir Prince of Cao, Gao, was once able to restrain Li Xilie with Jianghan troops; his authority and kindness live in men's hearts. Now, sending his son to command, there will surely be merit."

sentences.zh: 會道古自黔中觀察使入朝，乃代公綽，倍道入其軍，公綽惶遽出，財貲皆被奪。

translations.literal: It happened that Daogu came to court from Observation Commissioner of Qianzhong; he then replaced Gongchuo, entered his army by forced marches, and Gongchuo fled in panic—all his goods were seized.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that Daogu came to court from observation commissioner of Qianzhong; he then replaced Gongchuo, entered his army by forced marches, and Gongchuo fled in panic—all his goods were seized.

sentences.zh: 元和十二年，攻申州，破其郛，進圍中城。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Yuanhe he attacked Shenzhou, broke its outer wall, and advanced to besiege the inner city.
translations.idiomatic: In 817 he attacked Shenzhou, broke its outer wall, and advanced to besiege the inner city.

sentences.zh: 守卒夜驅女子登而噪，發懸門以出，道古眾亂，多死於賊。

translations.literal: The garrison troops by night drove women up on the walls to shout and make noise, then opened the drawbridge gate and sallied forth; Daogu's forces fell into disorder, and many died at the hands of the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison troops by night drove women up on the walls to shout and make noise, then opened the drawbridge gate and sallied forth; Daogu's forces fell into disorder, and many died at the hands of the rebels.

sentences.zh: 李聽守安州，未嘗敗，道古誣逐之。

translations.literal: Li Ting defended Anzhou and had never been defeated; Daogu slandered him and drove him away.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ting defended Anzhou without ever suffering defeat; Daogu slandered him and had him removed.

sentences.zh: 自將出穆陵關，士卒驕，不能制，又度支錢道古悉以饋權幸，故賜不給，其下怨怒，戰不甚力，賊亦易之。

translations.literal: He personally led troops out through Muleng Pass; the soldiers were arrogant and he could not control them. Moreover, the funds of the Revenue Commission Daogu entirely used to bribe the powerful and favored, so rewards were not issued; his subordinates resented and raged, fought without great effort, and the rebels also held him in contempt.
translations.idiomatic: He personally led troops out through Muleng Pass, but his soldiers were arrogant and beyond his control. Moreover, he diverted all funds from the Revenue Commission to bribe the powerful at court, so his troops received no rewards; his men grew resentful and fought half-heartedly, and the rebels held him in contempt.

sentences.zh: 故再入申，不能下，卒無功。

translations.literal: Therefore when he entered Shen again he could not take it, and in the end achieved nothing.
translations.idiomatic: When he attacked Shen again he could not capture it, and in the end achieved nothing.

sentences.zh: 淮西平，加檢校御史大夫，召為宗正卿、左金吾將軍。

translations.literal: When Huai-xi was pacified, he was given the additional title of Censor-in-Chief and summoned as Minister of the Imperial Clan and General of the Left Golden Crow Guard.
translations.idiomatic: After the pacification of Huai-xi, he was made acting Censor-in-Chief and recalled as Minister of the Imperial Clan and general of the Left Golden Crow Guard.

sentences.zh: 帝喜服餌，道古欲自媚，而所善柳泌自謂能化金為不死藥，乃因宰相皇甫镈以聞，俄會帝崩。

translations.literal: The emperor loved taking medicines; Daogu wished to ingratiate himself, and his favorite Liu Bi claimed he could transform gold into an elixir of immortality. Thereupon through Chancellor Huangfu Bo he reported it to the throne; shortly the emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor loved taking elixirs; Daogu wished to ingratiate himself, and his favorite Liu Bi claimed he could transform gold into an elixir of immortality. Through Chancellor Huangfu Bo he reported this to the throne; shortly thereafter the emperor died.

sentences.zh: 穆宗為太子，惡之，既立，誅泌，貶镈，斥道古為循州司馬。

translations.literal: When Muzong was crown prince he hated them; once enthroned he executed Bi, demoted Bo, and banished Daogu to be Vice-Prefect of Xunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Muzong was crown prince he hated them; once enthroned he executed Liu Bi, demoted Huangfu Bo, and banished Daogu to vice-prefect of Xunzhou.

sentences.zh: 終以服丹歐血死。

translations.literal: In the end, because of taking elixirs, he vomited blood and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he died vomiting blood from the elixirs he had taken.

sentences.zh: 長慶初，詔還其官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Changqing an edict restored his offices.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Changqing reign an edict restored his offices.

sentences.zh: 道古巧於宦，便佞傾下，遊公卿間，常與奕博，偽不勝，厚進所償，嗜利者多得其歡心，故少盜美名。

translations.literal: Daogu was skilled in office, facile and fawning toward subordinates; he moved among grandees and ministers, often playing chess and gambling, pretending not to win and lavishly advancing what he paid in compensation. Many who craved profit won his favor, and therefore he stole little good reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Daogu was skilled in courtcraft, facile and fawning toward subordinates. He moved among grandees and ministers, often playing chess and gambling while pretending to lose, then lavishly repaying his partners. Many who craved profit won his favor, and therefore he earned little good reputation.

sentences.zh: 及死，賣宅以葬。

translations.literal: When he died, his residence was sold to pay for his burial.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, his residence had to be sold to pay for his burial.
